description: Kubernetes 1.30 'Uwubernetes' brings 45 enhancements with a focus on security and observability. Contextual logging graduates to GA, container resource-based HPA reaches stable, and robust defaults improve security posture. Key features include recursive read-only mounts, job completion policy, and user namespaces beta.

securityInformation.title: Node Denial of Service via Kubelet Checkpoint API
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a large number of container checkpoint requests made to the unauthenticated kubelet read-only HTTP endpoint may cause a Node Denial of Service by filling the Node's disk.

securityInformation.title: Command Injection affecting Windows nodes via nodes/*/logs/query API
securityInformation.description:
A security vulnerability has been discovered in Kubernetes windows nodes
that could allow a user with the ability to query a node's '/logs' endpoint
to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

securityInformation.title: Incorrect permissions on Windows containers logs
securityInformation.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes clusters with Windows nodes
where BUILTIN\Users may be able to read container logs and NT
AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users may be able to modify container logs.

apiChange.description: "kubelet allowed specifying a custom root directory for pod logs (instead of the default /var/log/pods) using the `podLogsDir` key in kubelet configuration."
apiChange.author: mxpv
apiChange.userFacingChange:
kubelet: a custom root directory for pod logs (instead of default /var/log/pods) can be specified using the `podLogsDir`
key in kubelet configuration.

issueContext.title: Allow changing pod log directory
issueContext.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Kubelet currently hardcodes the path of pod log dirs here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L62

It would be nice if this was configurable.

**Why is this needed**:
Not having this configurable is quite annoying for locked-down systems with read-only filesystems where one needs tight controls over where software can write to.
Kubelet's RootDir is already configurable, but that is not particularly helpful if the log directory is hardcoded and no containers can start if the mkdir call for it fails.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet hard‑coded pod log directory to /var/log/pods, causing container start failures on systems where that path cannot be created (e.g., read‑only filesystems or environments requiring logs in a different location).
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kubelet on nodes where the default /var/log/pods path is unavailable or undesired, such as locked‑down environments, read‑only root filesystems, or installations that need logs in a custom location.
enrichment.fix: Added `podLogsDir` field to the Kubelet configuration allowing the root directory for pod logs to be overridden; kubelet now creates and writes logs under the configured path instead of the fixed /var/log/pods.
enrichment.impact: Operators can place pod logs on writable or secured storage, integrate with custom log collection pipelines, and run workloads on locked‑down nodes without failing due to log directory creation. Improves flexibility and compatibility with various deployment constraints.

apiChange.description: Text logging in Kubernetes components now uses [textlogger](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/klog/v2@v2.120.0/textlogger). The same split streams of info and error log entries with buffering of info entries is now also supported for text output (off by default, alpha feature). Previously, this was only supported for JSON. Performance is better also without split streams.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Text logging in Kubernetes components only supported JSON split streams of info and error with buffering; text output lacked this capability and had lower performance.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that emit logs (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl) and any tooling that consumes text logs.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes now uses the new textlogger implementation for text logging. It adds optional alpha support for split info/error streams with buffering for text output and improves baseline performance even when split streams are disabled.
enrichment.impact: Users can optionally get separate info and error log streams for text logs, improving log readability and analysis. The change also reduces logging overhead, benefiting all components that emit logs and improving overall cluster observability.

apiChange.description: "Implemented the `prescore` extension point for the `volumeBinding` plugin. It now returns skip if it doesn't do anything in Score."
apiChange.author: AxeZhan
apiChange.userFacingChange: Implement  `prescore` extension point for `volumeBinding` plugin. Return skip if it doesn't do anything in Score.

enrichment.problem: The volumeBinding scheduler plugin lacked a prescore extension point, causing the scheduler to treat the plugin as having performed scoring work even when it hadn't, which could lead to unnecessary processing or incorrect scheduling decisions for pods that require volume binding.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request PersistentVolumeClaims and rely on the volumeBinding plugin for node selection could have experienced sub‑optimal scheduling or unnecessary plugin execution.
enrichment.fix: Implemented the prescore extension point for the volumeBinding plugin and made it return a Skip result when the plugin has nothing to do during the Score phase.
enrichment.impact: Scheduler now correctly skips the volumeBinding plugin when no scoring is required, improving scheduling efficiency and preventing potential mis‑behaviour for pods using PersistentVolumeClaims.

apiChange.description: Users are now allowed to mutate `FSGroupPolicy` and `PodInfoOnMount` in `CSIDriver.Spec`.
apiChange.author: haoruan
apiChange.userFacingChange: Allow users to mutate FSGroupPolicy and PodInfoOnMount in CSIDriver.Spec

issueContext.title: Make specific fields inside CSIDriver.Spec mutable
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This is being proposed as change from https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2119

From` discussion among sig-storage, we agreed to make following fields inside `CSIDriver` mutable:

* FSGroupPolicy: it’s safe to be mutable
If two pods use the same volume, one of them can see it if fsGroup, the other without it. Seems to be OK.

* PodInfoOnMount: it’s safe to be mutable but Drivers must handle that



### Why is this needed?

We decided to do this, so as to support mutability of aforementioned fields as properly supported operation, rather than forcing users to delete and recreate `CSIDriver` object.

enrichment.problem: FSGroupPolicy and PodInfoOnMount fields in CSIDriver.Spec were immutable, requiring users to delete and recreate CSIDriver objects to change them, which caused unnecessary disruption and operational overhead.
enrichment.affected: Administrators and developers who manage CSIDriver resources for CSI drivers; any workloads that rely on mutable FSGroupPolicy or PodInfoOnMount settings.
enrichment.fix: The API server now allows these two fields to be mutated in-place. Validation has been updated so that updates to FSGroupPolicy and PodInfoOnMount are accepted without requiring object recreation.
enrichment.impact: Users can adjust FSGroupPolicy and PodInfoOnMount for existing CSIDriver objects without downtime, simplifying CSI driver configuration changes and reducing the risk of errors during re‑creation.

apiChange.description: Added consistent vanity import to files and provided tooling for verifying and updating them.
apiChange.author: jcchavezs

issueContext.title: Automate vanity imports update and verify
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Vanity imports to all packages, for example

```
package validatingwebhookconfiguration
```
into
```
package validatingwebhookconfiguration // import "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/registry/admissionregistration/validatingwebhookconfiguration"
```

**IMPORTANT:** Kubernetes repository already uses vanity imports, we just need to provide a check so new code includes it and provide a tool for users to regenerate vanity imports.

### Why is this needed?

Following https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/68231, vanity imports improves code navegability for a codebase with many packages as otherwise you need to figure out what the package is, the vanity URL and probably handtype the import path.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source files lacked consistent vanity import comments, making it harder for developers to navigate packages and preventing automated checks from ensuring these comments are present.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes developers and CI pipelines that build or test the Kubernetes codebase; downstream contributors who rely on correct package import paths.
enrichment.fix: Added a uniform vanity import comment to all relevant Go files and introduced tooling that can verify the presence of these comments and automatically update/regenerate them across the codebase.
enrichment.impact: Improves code readability and navigation for developers, enables CI to enforce the vanity import style, and reduces manual effort and errors when adding new packages.

apiChange.description: When scheduling a mix of pods using `ResourceClaims` and others that don't, scheduling a pod with `ResourceClaims` has a lower impact on scheduling latency.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: When scheduling a mixture of pods using ResourceClaims and others which don't, scheduling a pod with ResourceClaims impacts scheduling latency less.

enrichment.problem: When a cluster schedules a mix of pods that use ResourceClaims and pods that do not, the presence of ResourceClaim pods caused higher scheduling latency, slowing down overall pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that include both ResourceClaim‑using pods and non‑ResourceClaim pods, especially in large or latency‑sensitive clusters.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler was updated to treat pods that use ResourceClaims more efficiently, so that scheduling those pods now has a smaller impact on overall scheduling latency when mixed with other pods.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that run both ResourceClaim‑based pods and regular pods will see reduced scheduling latency, leading to faster pod startups and improved throughput for workloads that depend on dynamic resource claims.

apiChange.description: "Added the `CEL` library for IP Addresses and CIDRs. This was made available for use starting from version `1.31`."
apiChange.author: JoelSpeed
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add CEL library for IP Addresses and CIDRs. This will not be available for use until 1.31.

enrichment.problem: There was no built‑in CEL (Common Expression Language) library providing functions for handling IP addresses and CIDR blocks, forcing users to implement custom logic for validation and policy checks.
enrichment.affected: Developers and cluster operators who author CEL expressions for admission, validation, or policy enforcement that need IP/CIDR handling.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new CEL library that adds native IP address and CIDR manipulation functions. The library is shipped with Kubernetes and becomes usable starting with version 1.31.
enrichment.impact: Users can now write simpler, more reliable CEL expressions for network‑related validation (e.g., admission controllers, CRD validation, policy engines) without rolling their own code, reducing bugs and development effort.

apiChange.description: Contextual logging is now in beta and enabled by default. Check out the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3077) and [official documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging) for more details.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: Contextual logging is now beta and enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: Contextual information (e.g., pod name, namespace, UID) was not included in component logs by default, requiring users to manually enable the alpha feature to get richer logs for troubleshooting.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters; users who rely on component logs for debugging and monitoring are now provided with contextual data automatically.
enrichment.fix: Promoted contextual logging to beta and enabled it by default for all core control‑plane and node components, automatically adding contextual fields to log entries.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and developers receive richer, structured logs out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying debugging and observability without extra configuration.

apiChange.description: Added to `MutableFeatureGate` the ability to override the default setting of feature gates, to allow default-enabling a feature on a component-by-component basis instead of for all affected components simultaneously.
apiChange.author: benluddy
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added to MutableFeatureGate the ability to override the default setting of feature gates, to allow default-enabling a feature on a component-by-component basis instead of for all affected components simultaneously.

enrichment.problem: Feature gates could only be default-enabled globally, requiring all components that recognize a feature to be enabled at once. There was no way to set a default value per individual component, forcing users to manually override each component's flag.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and component developers who need to enable a feature by default for only a subset of components (e.g., kubelet, kube‑apiserver, scheduler, controller‑manager).
enrichment.fix: MutableFeatureGate now supports overriding the default value of a feature gate on a per‑component basis. Operators can declare a default enabled state for a specific component while leaving the global default unchanged.
enrichment.impact: Allows finer‑grained control of feature rollout, simplifying component‑specific default enablement and reducing configuration friction for cluster operators and developers.

apiChange.description: Alpha support for field selectors on custom resources has been added. With the `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` feature gate enabled, the CustomResourceDefinition API now allows specifying `selectableFields`. Listing a field there enables filtering custom resources for that CustomResourceDefinition in list or watch requests.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added alpha support for field selectors on custom resources.
Provided that the `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` feature gate is enabled, the CustomResourceDefinition
API now lets you specify `selectableFields`. Listing a field there allows filtering custom resources for that
CustomResourceDefinition in **list** or **watch** requests.

enrichment.problem: Custom resources could not be filtered with field selectors, forcing users to retrieve all resources and filter client‑side, which is inefficient for large CRD sets.
enrichment.affected: Operators and developers who create or consume CustomResourceDefinitions that need selective list/watch behavior; any workloads that generate large numbers of custom resources.
enrichment.fix: Introduces alpha support for field selectors on custom resources. When the `CustomResourceFieldSelectors` feature gate is enabled, CRD definitions can list `selectableFields`. Those fields become usable in list and watch requests, enabling server‑side filtering.
enrichment.impact: Allows clients and kubectl to efficiently query or watch only the desired custom resources, reducing load on the API server and network, and enabling new tooling scenarios that rely on field‑selector semantics.

apiChange.description: The `kube_codegen` tool now ignores the vendor folder during code generation.
apiChange.author: jparrill
apiChange.userFacingChange: Adds a rule on the kube_codegen tool to ignore vendor folder during the code generation.

enrichment.problem: The kube_codegen tool previously traversed into the vendor directory, causing it to generate code for vendored dependencies that should be ignored.
enrichment.affected: Users of the kube_codegen tool (e.g., API client library maintainers and CI jobs that generate code) were generating unwanted files from vendored code.
enrichment.fix: A new rule is added to kube_codegen so that it skips the vendor folder during code generation.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines that use kube_codegen will see cleaner output, avoid unnecessary generated files, and experience faster code‑generation runs.

apiChange.description: In kubelet configuration, the `.memorySwap.swapBehavior` field now accepts a new value `NoSwap`, which becomes the default if unspecified. The previously accepted `UnlimitedSwap` value has been dropped.
apiChange.author: kannon92
apiChange.userFacingChange: kubelet: the `.memorySwap.swapBehavior` field in kubelet configuration accepts a new value `NoSwap` and makes this the default if unspecified; the previously accepted `UnlimitedSwap` value has been dropped.

enrichment.problem: The kubelet configuration field `.memorySwap.swapBehavior` previously accepted the value `UnlimitedSwap`. With the change, `UnlimitedSwap` is removed and the new value `NoSwap` becomes the default when the field is unspecified, potentially breaking existing configurations that rely on the old default or explicitly set `UnlimitedSwap`.
enrichment.affected: Users who configure kubelet memory swap behavior, especially those with `UnlimitedSwap` set or relying on the previous default swap behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new enum value `NoSwap` for `.memorySwap.swapBehavior` and makes it the default. The deprecated `UnlimitedSwap` value is removed, so users must update any kubelet config files that reference it.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that used swap memory (either via explicit `UnlimitedSwap` or by relying on the previous default) will stop using swap, which can lead to higher memory pressure and possible OOM situations for workloads that depended on swap. Administrators need to review and adjust kubelet configurations accordingly.

apiChange.description: Added a CBOR implementation of `runtime.Serializer`. Until CBOR graduates to Alpha, API servers will refuse to start if configured with CBOR support.
apiChange.author: benluddy

enrichment.problem: API servers would fail to start if a user enabled CBOR serialization before the feature reached Alpha, making the configuration unusable.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the API server is configured with CBOR support prior to its Alpha graduation would fail to start.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a CBOR runtime.Serializer and added a guard that rejects CBOR support in API server configuration until the feature graduates to Alpha.
enrichment.impact: Lays the groundwork for future CBOR support while preventing accidental misconfiguration that would stop the API server from starting.

apiChange.description: Aggregated discovery supports both `v2beta1` and v2 types and feature is promoted to GA.
apiChange.author: Jefftree
apiChange.userFacingChange: Aggregated discovery supports both v2beta1 and v2 types and feature is promoted to GA

enrichment.problem: Aggregated discovery only supported the older v2beta1 discovery format, causing incompatibility for clients expecting the newer v2 format and requiring a feature gate to enable the functionality.
enrichment.affected: Users of the Kubernetes discovery API, especially those interacting with aggregated API servers or custom resource definitions, were affected by the limited version support.
enrichment.fix: The implementation was updated to handle both v2beta1 and v2 discovery types, and the aggregated discovery feature has been promoted to GA, making it stable and enabled by default.
enrichment.impact: Clients and tools that rely on discovery can now use either version without extra configuration, improving compatibility and stability. The GA promotion signals that the feature is production‑ready and no longer experimental.

apiChange.description:
Added audienceMatchPolicy field to AuthenticationConfiguration and support for configuring multiple audiences.
The "audienceMatchPolicy" can be empty (or unset) when a single audience is specified in the "audiences" field.
The "audienceMatchPolicy" must be set to "MatchAny" when multiple audiences are specified in the "audiences" field.
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added audienceMatchPolicy field to AuthenticationConfiguration and support for configuring multiple audiences.

- The "audienceMatchPolicy" can be empty (or unset) when a single audience is specified in the "audiences" field.
- The "audienceMatchPolicy" must be set to "MatchAny" when multiple audiences are specified in the "audiences" field.

enrichment.problem: AuthenticationConfiguration only supported a single audience, making it impossible to configure multiple audiences for token validation.
enrichment.affected: Users configuring AuthenticationConfiguration for API server authentication, especially those needing multi‑audience token validation.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an optional audienceMatchPolicy field and extended the audiences list to accept multiple values. When multiple audiences are provided, the policy must be set to MatchAny; for a single audience the field can be omitted.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now validate tokens against multiple audiences, enabling more flexible and secure authentication scenarios without requiring custom code or work‑arounds.

apiChange.description: "`readOnly` volumes now support recursive read-only mounts for kernel versions >= 5.12."
apiChange.author: AkihiroSuda
apiChange.userFacingChange: Support Recursive Read-only (RRO) mounts  (KEP-3857)

enrichment.problem: ReadOnly volumes could not be mounted recursively as read‑only on kernels >= 5.12, leading to mount failures or unintended writable access for subpaths.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use readOnly volumes on nodes running Linux kernel 5.12+ were unable to perform recursive read‑only mounts.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now enables Recursive Read‑Only (RRO) mounts for ReadOnly volumes when the underlying kernel supports it (kernel version 5.12 or newer).
enrichment.impact: Workloads that rely on read‑only volume semantics, especially those using sub‑directory mounts, now function correctly on newer Linux kernels, improving security and stability of storage usage.

apiChange.description: "cri-api: Implemented KEP-3857: Recursive Read-only (RRO) mounts."
apiChange.author: AkihiroSuda
apiChange.userFacingChange: cri-api: KEP-3857: Recursive Read-only (RRO) mounts

enrichment.problem: Containers could not request recursive read‑only mounts via the CRI, making it impossible to enforce read‑only access for entire mount sub‑trees and limiting security/privilege isolation scenarios.
enrichment.affected: Pod specifications that rely on mount options, especially those using readOnlyRootFilesystem or custom volume mounts, and container runtimes that interact with the CRI.
enrichment.fix: Implemented KEP‑3857 in the CRI API to support Recursive Read‑Only (RRO) mount options. The kubelet and runtimes can now pass a flag indicating that a mount and all of its child mounts must be read‑only, and the runtime enforces this behavior.
enrichment.impact: Allows workloads to harden file‑system access, improving security and compliance for pods that need strict read‑only filesystems. Enables use‑cases such as shared read‑only data volumes, reducing risk of accidental writes.

apiChange.description: "Added (alpha) support for the `managedBy` field on Jobs. Jobs with a custom value of this field - any value other than `kubernetes.io/job-controller` - were skipped by the job controller, and their reconciliation was delegated to an external controller, indicated by the value of the field. Jobs that didn't have this field at all, or where the field value was the reserved string `kubernetes.io/job-controller`, were reconciled by the built-in job controller."
apiChange.author: mimowo
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added (alpha) support for the managedBy field on Jobs. Jobs with a custom value of this field - any
value other than `kubernetes.io/job-controller` - are skipped by the job controller, and their
reconciliation is delegated to an external controller, indicated by the value of the field. Jobs that
don't have this field at all, or where the field value is the reserved string `kubernetes.io/job-controller`,
are reconciled by the built-in job controller.

enrichment.problem: Custom controllers could not mark a Job as owned by an external controller, so the built‑in job controller always reconciled every Job, leading to conflicts or duplicate handling for Jobs managed outside of the default controller.
enrichment.affected: Users running custom Job controllers or operators that need exclusive control over Job lifecycle; clusters where the default job controller would otherwise interfere with external job management.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an alpha `managedBy` field on the Job API. When the field is set to any value other than the reserved `kubernetes.io/job-controller`, the built‑in job controller skips reconciliation of that Job and delegates management to the external controller identified by the field value. Jobs without the field or with the reserved value continue to be reconciled by the built‑in controller.
enrichment.impact: Allows operators and custom controllers to safely manage Jobs without interference from the default job controller, enabling clearer ownership, reducing conflicts, and paving the way for richer batch‑job ecosystems.

apiChange.description: "The `StorageVersionMigration` API, previously available as a Custom Resource Definition (CRD), is now a built-in API in Kubernetes."
apiChange.author: nilekhc
apiChange.userFacingChange: The `StorageVersionMigration` API, which was previously available as a Custom Resource Definition (CRD), is now a built-in API in Kubernetes.

issueContext.title: Initial implementation of moving Storage Version Migrator in-tree
issueContext.body:
Ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4240

/sig api-machinery
/assign

enrichment.problem: StorageVersionMigration was only available as a Custom Resource Definition, requiring manual installation and management, which added complexity and could lead to missing or out‑of‑date CRDs during upgrades.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that use or plan to use the StorageVersionMigration API, as well as operators who previously had to install the CRD manually.
enrichment.fix: The StorageVersionMigration API is promoted to a built‑in, in‑tree API. It is now served directly by the kube‑apiserver and managed by the built‑in storage‑version‑migrator controller, removing the need for a separate CRD installation.
enrichment.impact: Clusters get the StorageVersionMigration capability automatically, simplifying installation, upgrade and operational processes. Users no longer need to install or maintain a separate CRD, reducing the risk of version skew and ensuring the migrator works out‑of‑the‑box.

apiChange.description:
Added a alpha feature, behind the `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation` feature gate.
When that gate is enabled, Kubernetes allows almost all printable ASCII characters to be used in the names
of environment variables for containers in Pods.
apiChange.author: HirazawaUi
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added a alpha feature, behind the `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation` feature gate.
When that gate is enabled, Kubernetes allows almost all printable ASCII characters to be used in the names
of environment variables for containers in Pods.

issueContext.title: Environment variables containing colon not allowed
issueContext.body:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY! 

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind feature

**Problem:**
Kubernetes does not support `:` in environment variables. I can see that the subject has recently been discussed in [PR #48986](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/48986). .NET Core uses `:` to replace config variables as mentioned in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/48986#issuecomment-318628326). The limitation in kubernetes requires me to perform some ugly hacks to override the config values.

**Proposed Solution:**
I'm in favor of the sentiment that kubernetes should not censor environment variables at all, but specifically I would like `:` to be allowed.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes restricted environment variable names to a limited character set, disallowing many printable ASCII characters such as ':'. This prevented workloads (e.g., .NET Core applications) from using their native configuration conventions and required work‑arounds.
enrichment.affected: Users running Pods that need environment variable names containing special printable ASCII characters (e.g., .NET Core apps, Windows workloads).
enrichment.fix: Introduced the alpha feature gate `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation`. When enabled, the API server relaxes validation and permits almost all printable ASCII characters in container environment variable names.
enrichment.impact: Allows applications to pass environment variables with characters like ':' directly, simplifying configuration management and reducing hacky work‑arounds. Improves compatibility for Windows containers and frameworks that rely on special characters.

apiChange.description: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy was promoted to GA and will be `enabled` by default.
apiChange.author: cici37
apiChange.userFacingChange: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is promoted to GA and will be enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy was only available as a beta feature and required manual enablement, making it harder for clusters to enforce validation policies consistently.
enrichment.affected: All clusters that upgrade to this version and any workloads relying on admission validation will now have the policy enforced by default.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to GA and is now enabled by default in the API server, removing the need for manual activation.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgrading to this release automatically get validation admission policies without extra configuration, improving security and reliability of admission control across workloads.

apiChange.description: "Added alpha-level support for the SuccessPolicy in Jobs."
apiChange.author: tenzen-y
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add alpha-level support for the SuccessPolicy in Jobs

enrichment.problem: Jobs only had a single success condition (all pods must succeed), so users could not define alternative success criteria for workloads that should be considered successful under different conditions.
enrichment.affected: Users creating Batch/v1 Job resources who need non‑default success criteria (e.g., any pod succeeding).
enrichment.fix: Adds an alpha-level `SuccessPolicy` field to the Job spec, allowing users to specify how a Job is deemed successful (e.g., any pod succeeds). Updates the Job API, validation, and controller logic to honor the new policy.
enrichment.impact: Provides flexible job completion semantics, enabling patterns such as "first-success" jobs without custom wrappers, and gives users more control over workload success tracking.

apiChange.description: Structured Authentication Configuration now supports configuring multiple JWT authenticators. The maximum allowed JWT authenticators in the authentication configuration is 64.
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added support for configuring multiple JWT authenticators in Structured Authentication Configuration. The maximum allowed JWT authenticators in the authentication configuration is 64.

enrichment.problem: Structured Authentication Configuration only allowed a single JWT authenticator, preventing clusters from validating tokens issued by multiple providers.
enrichment.affected: Users configuring the Structured Authentication Configuration for the kube-apiserver who need to handle multiple JWT issuers.
enrichment.fix: Extended the authentication configuration schema to accept a list of JWT authenticators and raised the hard limit to 64 entries.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now natively validate tokens from many issuers (e.g., multiple OIDC providers) without custom webhook hacks, simplifying security setups and scaling auth configurations.

apiChange.description: AppArmor profiles can now be configured through fields on the `PodSecurityContext` and container `SecurityContext`. The beta AppArmor annotations are deprecated, and AppArmor status is no longer included in the node ready condition.
apiChange.author: tallclair
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- AppArmor profiles can now be configured through fields on the PodSecurityContext and container SecurityContext.
- The beta AppArmor annotations are deprecated.
- AppArmor status is no longer included in the node ready condition

enrichment.problem: AppArmor could only be configured using beta annotations, which were not first‑class API fields and caused confusion. The node ready condition also reported AppArmor status, leading to noisy node health signals.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use AppArmor profiles for pods and containers, and any tooling that relied on the beta annotations or node ready condition for AppArmor status.
enrichment.fix: Added explicit fields for AppArmor profile selection in PodSecurityContext and container SecurityContext, deprecated the old beta annotations, and removed AppArmor status from the node ready condition. The API schema and kubelet enforcement were updated accordingly.
enrichment.impact: Users can now configure AppArmor profiles via the stable API, simplifying management and improving consistency. Deprecating the annotations clears the path for GA support, and removing the status from the node ready condition reduces false‑positive node‑unready alerts.

apiChange.description:
Graduated support for `minDomains` in pod topology spread constraints, to general availability.
The `MinDomainsInPodTopologySpread` feature gate no longer has any effect, and the field is
always available within the Pod and PodTemplate APIs.
apiChange.author: sanposhiho
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Graduated support for `minDomains` in pod topology spread constraints, to general availability.
The `MinDomainsInPodTopologySpread` feature gate no longer has any effect, and the field is
always available within the Pod and PodTemplate APIs.

enrichment.problem: The `minDomains` field for pod topology spread constraints was behind the `MinDomainsInPodTopologySpread` feature gate, so it was unavailable by default and could not be used reliably in production.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on pod topology spread constraints (pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.) and needs the `minDomains` capability for placement.
enrichment.fix: Graduated `minDomains` to general availability: the feature gate is removed and the field is always present in Pod and PodTemplate specs.
enrichment.impact: Users can now specify a minimum number of zones/domains for spreading pods, giving better control over pod distribution and high‑availability placement without needing a feature gate.

apiChange.description: Added a new (alpha) field, `trafficDistribution`, to the Service `spec` to express preferences for traffic distribution to endpoints. Enabled through the `ServiceTrafficDistribution` feature gate.
apiChange.author: gauravkghildiyal
apiChange.userFacingChange:
A new (alpha) field, `trafficDistribution`, has been added to the Service `spec`.
This field provides a way to express preferences for how traffic is distributed to the endpoints for a Service.
It can be enabled through the `ServiceTrafficDistribution` feature gate.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes services had no way to specify preferences for how traffic should be distributed among a Service's endpoints, limiting control over routing behavior such as weighted or topology-aware load‑balancing.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses a Service and wants to control how traffic is split among its endpoints. Cluster administrators enabling the feature gate will see the new field in Service manifests.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new alpha field `trafficDistribution` in the Service spec. When the `ServiceTrafficDistribution` feature gate is enabled, users can set this field to express desired traffic distribution preferences for the Service's endpoints.
enrichment.impact: Provides operators and developers with fine‑grained control over Service traffic routing, enabling use‑cases like weighted load‑balancing or topology‑aware distribution without external proxies. The change is optional and gated, so existing clusters are unaffected unless the feature is turned on.

apiChange.description: "Dynamic Resource Allocation: DRA drivers can now use "structured parameters" to let the scheduler handle claim allocation."
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: Dynamic Resource Allocation: DRA drivers may now use "structured parameters" to let the scheduler handle claim allocation.

enrichment.problem: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) drivers could only pass opaque parameters, preventing the scheduler from understanding resource specifics and making informed claim allocation decisions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using DRA drivers and workloads that request DRA claims; scheduler behavior is changed to handle the new structured parameters.
enrichment.fix: Introduce support for structured parameters in DRA drivers, allowing them to describe resource details in a schema that the scheduler can parse and use to allocate claims automatically.
enrichment.impact: Schedulers can now make placement decisions based on rich resource information, simplifying driver implementations and improving workload scheduling for resources like GPUs, accelerators, or custom storage classes.

apiChange.description: The JWT authenticator configuration set via the `--authentication-config` flag is now dynamically reloaded as the file changes on disk.
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange: JWT authenticator config set via the --authentication-config flag is now dynamically reloaded as the file changes on disk.

issueContext.title: [StructuredAuthenticationConfig] Implement reloading of configuration
issueContext.body:
/sig auth
/assign
/triage accepted

enrichment.problem: The JWT authenticator configuration provided via the --authentication-config flag was loaded only at API server start, requiring a restart to apply any changes to the file.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the kube-apiserver with the --authentication-config flag for JWT authentication. Any workload relying on up‑to‑date JWT validation is affected.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a file‑watcher that detects modifications to the JWT auth config file and reloads the authenticator dynamically without needing to restart the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can rotate JWT keys or update authentication settings instantly, reducing downtime and improving security posture for clusters that use JWT authentication.

apiChange.description: "Structured Authentication Configuration now supports `DiscoveryURL`. If specified, `discoveryURL` overrides the URL used to fetch discovery information. This is for scenarios where the well-known and jwks endpoints are hosted at a different location than the issuer (such as locally in the cluster)."
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Structured Authentication Configuration now supports `DiscoveryURL`. 
discoveryURL if specified, overrides the URL used to fetch discovery information. 
This is for scenarios where the well-known and jwks endpoints are hosted at a different
location than the issuer (such as locally in the cluster).

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes could only fetch OpenID Connect discovery information from the issuer URL, making it impossible to use scenarios where the well-known and JWKS endpoints are hosted at a different location (e.g., a local endpoint inside the cluster).
enrichment.affected: Users who configure Structured Authentication for OIDC providers where the discovery and JWKS endpoints are not co‑located with the issuer—such as deployments that expose these endpoints inside the cluster.
enrichment.fix: Add a `discoveryURL` field to Structured Authentication Configuration. When set, this URL overrides the default discovery location, allowing the API server to retrieve discovery data from an alternate endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now point the authentication discovery process to custom or locally hosted endpoints, simplifying setups that separate the issuer from its discovery/JWKS services and reducing network dependencies.

apiChange.description: "Promoted `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` to GA. The feature is now stable, and the feature gate is now locked to default."
apiChange.author: ivelichkovich
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions to GA. The feature is now stable and the feature gate is now locked to default.

enrichment.problem: Admission webhook match conditions were only available in Beta and required the AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions feature gate to be manually enabled, causing extra steps and potential incompatibility for users wanting to use conditional admission webhook logic.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use admission webhooks and want to apply match conditions. Existing webhook configurations that already enabled the feature gate will continue to work unchanged.
enrichment.fix: Promoted AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions to GA and locked the feature gate to its default (enabled) state, making match conditions a stable, always‑on capability of the API server admission webhook framework.
enrichment.impact: Users can now rely on match conditions in admission webhooks without extra configuration, improving reliability and simplifying webhook implementations. The change is backward compatible and requires no action from clusters already using the feature.

apiChange.description: The API server now detects and fails on startup if there are conflicting issuers between JWT authenticators and service account configurations. Previously, such configurations would run but could be inconsistently effective depending on the credential.
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange: Conflicting issuers between JWT authenticators and service account config are now detected and fail on API server startup.  Previously such a config would run but would be inconsistently effective depending on the credential.

enrichment.problem: When the API server was configured with JWT token authenticators and a service account token issuer that used different issuers, the server started without error but authentication behaved inconsistently, potentially accepting or rejecting credentials unpredictably.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that configured both JWT authenticators and service account token issuers with differing issuer strings. The issue manifested during API server startup and could lead to unpredictable authentication outcomes.
enrichment.fix: The API server now validates the issuer settings on startup and aborts if a conflict between JWT authenticators and the service account configuration is detected.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with mismatched issuer settings will fail to start, preventing accidental insecure or broken authentication configurations. Administrators must align issuer values, ensuring reliable and secure authentication for all workloads.

apiChange.description: OIDC authentication will now fail if the username asserted based on a CEL expression config is the empty string.  Previously the request would be authenticated with the username set to the empty string.
apiChange.author: enj

enrichment.problem: OIDC authentication accepted tokens that resulted in an empty username when a CEL expression was used for username mapping, leading to ambiguous or unintended identities.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using OIDC authentication with a CEL expression for username that could evaluate to an empty string.
enrichment.fix: The authentication flow now rejects tokens that would produce an empty username, causing the request to fail instead of authenticating with an empty username.
enrichment.impact: Improves security and correctness of OIDC authentication by preventing ambiguous user identities, avoiding potential permission misassignments for clusters using custom CEL username mappings.

apiChange.description:
Graduated pod scheduling gates to general availability.
The `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate no longer has any effect, and the
`.spec.schedulingGates` field is always available within the Pod and PodTemplate APIs.

Graduated pod scheduling gates to general availability.
The `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate no longer has any effect, and the
`.spec.schedulingGates` field is always available within the Pod and PodTemplate APIs.

enrichment.problem: The `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate controlled the availability of the `.spec.schedulingGates` field. When the gate was disabled, the field was not present in Pod and PodTemplate specs, causing confusion and requiring explicit feature gate management for using scheduling gates.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that creates or updates Pods/PodTemplates and previously relied on the `PodSchedulingReadiness` feature gate. Controllers, CI pipelines, or manifests that toggled the gate need to remove it.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been removed and the `.spec.schedulingGates` field is now permanently available in the Pod and PodTemplate APIs, making pod scheduling gates generally available.

apiChange.description: kube-apiserver: the AuthorizationConfiguration type accepted in `--authorization-config` files has been promoted to `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`.
apiChange.author: liggitt

apiChange.description: "kube-apiserver: the AuthenticationConfiguration type accepted in `--authentication-config` files has been promoted to `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`."
apiChange.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver only accepted an unversioned AuthenticationConfiguration type in files passed via the --authentication-config flag, limiting validation and future compatibility.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that uses the kube-apiserver with the --authentication-config flag for custom authentication configuration.

apiChange.description: The `StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration` feature is now beta and enabled.
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange: The StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature is now beta and enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature was previously alpha and disabled by default, requiring manual enablement. Clusters without it could not use the new structured authentication config and needed to opt‑in.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kube-apiserver that rely on authentication configuration; any workloads that depend on authentication semantics may see changed behavior.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to beta and is now enabled by default, so the API server will automatically use the structured authentication configuration without additional flags.

apiChange.description:
"When configuring a JWT authenticator:

If `username.expression` used 'claims.email', then 'claims.email_verified' must have been used in `username.expression` or `extra[*].valueExpression` or `claimValidationRules[*].expression`. An example claim validation rule expression that matches the validation automatically applied when `username.claim` is set to 'email' is 'claims.?email_verified.orValue(true)'."
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange:
When configuring a JWT authenticator:

If username.expression uses 'claims.email', then 'claims.email_verified' must be used in
username.expression or extra[*].valueExpression or claimValidationRules[*].expression.
An example claim validation rule expression that matches the validation automatically
applied when username.claim is set to 'email' is 'claims.?email_verified.orValue(true) == true'.

issueContext.title: Document `email_verified` check when CEL expression is used in authentication configuration
issueContext.body:
When the `email` claim is used directly, we perform a custom check against the `email_verified` claim if it is present:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9043ce05c125091c0cb5519206fd90d311abd8c8/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/plugin/pkg/authenticator/token/oidc/oidc.go#L779-L793

I do not think this type of check makes sense via the CEL based config, but we should document how to perform a similar validation since that check is lost if moving a config to use CEL expressions and the admin is unaware of the implicit `email_verified` check.

cc @aramase @liggitt

enrichment.problem: When configuring a JWT authenticator with a CEL expression that references `claims.email`, the built‑in check that also verifies `claims.email_verified` is not applied. This allowed admins to unintentionally accept unverified email addresses as usernames.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators who configure JWT authentication with CEL expressions that use the `email` claim without also checking `email_verified`.
enrichment.fix: The authenticator now validates that any expression using `claims.email` must also reference `claims.email_verified` – either in `username.expression`, any `extra[*].valueExpression`, or a `claimValidationRules[*].expression`. An example validation rule (`claims.?email_verified.orValue(true) == true`) is provided.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that email‑based usernames are only accepted when the email is verified, preventing potential security bypasses and aligning CEL‑based configs with the previous implicit verification behavior.

apiChange.description: "Kubelet would fail if NodeSwap was used with LimitedSwap and cgroupv1 node."
apiChange.author: kannon92
apiChange.userFacingChange: Kubelet should fail if NodeSwap is used with LimitedSwap and cgroupv1 node.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet crashes when a node is configured with NodeSwap and LimitedSwap while using cgroupv1, leading to node instability.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running cgroup v1 that have both NodeSwap enabled and LimitedSwap configured; workloads on those nodes are impacted by the kubelet failure.
enrichment.fix: Added validation that detects the unsupported combination (NodeSwap + LimitedSwap on cgroupv1) and makes kubelet fail fast with a clear error message, preventing undefined behavior.
enrichment.impact: Operators receive an explicit error instead of an unexpected kubelet failure, allowing them to correct the configuration before the node becomes unusable.

bugOrRegression.description: Enabled concurrent log rotation in kubelet. You can now configure the maximum number of concurrent rotations with the `containerLogMaxWorkers` setting, and adjust the monitoring interval with `containerLogMonitorInterval`.
bugOrRegression.author: harshanarayana
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Enabled a mechanism for concurrent log rotatation via `kubelet` using a configuration entity of `containerLogMaxWorkers` which controls the maximum number of concurrent rotation that can be performed and an interval configuration of `containerLogMonitorInterval` that can aid is configuring the monitoring duration to best suite your cluster's log generation standards.

issueContext.title: Kubelet does not respect container-log-max-size on time, during heavy log writes from container
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We are running a Statefulset that logs pretty aggressively on disk. The rate is around 6M/second. The kubelet configs around container log management are set to:
- container-log-max-files: 5
- container-log-max-size: 50Mi

We are running with containerd as the CRI on Kubernetes version 1.20. 


For this specific workload, we notice that the logs DO NOT get rotated upon hitting the 50Mi limit. Instead, the rotation happens at a much later size, depending on the number of containers/Pods on the node. In some extreme cases, if there are several Pods that are aggressively logging to disk, on the same node, then the kubelet lets the log size grow up to several tens of GBs before noticing that the log size has grown out of control. Then, it steps in to rotate the logs (compress and replace). 

This problem is letting nodes consume Terabytes of disk space, as opposed to a few hundred MBs of data for logging. 

### What did you expect to happen?

container logs should be rotated out as specified in the container-log-max-size kubelet configuration.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

My coworker (Venkata Gunapati) has a simple repro for the issue using the following Statefulset spec.

Upon applying this spec, we observe that the Pod/container's log file grow beyond 50Mi to uptown 256Mi, before rotating the logs. It is obvious how the problem gets extreme when dozens of such Pods run on the same node.


```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: logging-test
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logging-test
  serviceName: "logging-test"
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: logging-test
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
      containers:
      - name: logging-test
        command: ["sh", "-c", "i=1; while [ $i -le 100  ]; do j=1; while [ $j -le 2000 ]; do echo 2022-06-16T20:02:18,308+0000 2gEAAAABu0zlAy3NjPX1DPttWcZsBs

enrichment.problem: Under heavy log generation, kubelet rotated container logs sequentially, causing it to miss the configured `containerLogMaxSize` limit. Logs could grow many times larger (tens of GB) before rotation, leading to disk exhaustion on nodes.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with containers that produce high‑rate logs; especially workloads like statefulsets with aggressive logging.
enrichment.fix: Added a concurrent log‑rotation mechanism to kubelet. The new `containerLogMaxWorkers` setting caps the number of simultaneous rotations, and `containerLogMonitorInterval` lets users tune how often log files are scanned. This ensures log rotation respects size limits even under high write rates.
enrichment.impact: Prevents nodes from running out of disk space due to unrotated logs, improves reliability for workloads that generate large volumes of logs (e.g., statefulsets), and reduces latency of log‑rotation operations.

bugOrRegression.description: "Fixed an issue where mount points could become local without calling `NodePublishVolume` after node rebooting."
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: fix: Mount point may become local without calling NodePublishVolume after node rebooting.

issueContext.title: Mount point may become local without calling `NodePublishVolume` after node rebooting
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

This issue is very similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, they have the same symptom: remote volumes of the pods are becoming local mount point after rebooting the Node. And this issue is triggered by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513.

The difference is that in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, kubelet didn't call `NodeStageVolume`, so the global mount point is local, but it will still call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod to bind mount the pod volume to the global mount point. Whereas in this issue, kubelet neither call `NodeStageVolume` globally nor call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod. 

This is more harmful: After writing some data to the pod volume, pod can't be deleted because kubelet encounter `directory not empty` error while unmounting the pod volume:
 
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/44308864/b1cc4e04-15ac-4730-a862-54eddf2a4960)


Reproduce steps:
1. Create a cluster with one Node
2. Create a deployment with **two replicas**(say `pod-1` and `pod-2`) using Non-attachable volume (for example Azurefile)
3. Shutdown the Node
4. Delete `pod-1` with option `--force` (Use force deletion to simulate the situation that mount point was left over before rebooting the Node.)
5. Bring back the Node
6. `pod-2` is always in Running state, however, after rebooting, it won't call `NodePublishVolume` and the volume it uses is local volume.

### What did you expect to happen?

`pod-2` should call `NodePublishVolume`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

As mentioned above.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"24", GitVersion:"v1.24.4", GitCommit:"95ee5ab382d64cfe6c28967f36b53970b8374491", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-08-17T18:54:23Z", G

enrichment.problem: After a node reboot, kubelet may treat remote CSI volumes as local mount points without invoking NodePublishVolume (or NodeStageVolume). This leaves stale mount points, causing pod volume deletions to fail with "directory not empty" errors and leaves the volume in an inconsistent state.
enrichment.affected: Pods using CSI non‑attachable volumes on nodes that have been rebooted, especially when a pod was force‑deleted before the reboot. The issue manifested as mount points becoming local and pod deletions failing.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now ensures that, after a node restart, it re-invokes the CSI NodePublishVolume (and NodeStageVolume when needed) for volumes that were previously mounted. This prevents stale local mount points and guarantees proper cleanup of pod volumes.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use non‑attachable CSI volumes (e.g., AzureFile) will no longer get stuck in a terminating state after a node reboot. Deleting pods will correctly unmount and clean up volumes, avoiding data‑consistency issues and reducing operational overhead for cluster operators.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed Windows credential provider, cannot find binary. Windows credential provider binary path may have ".exe" suffix so it is better to use `LookPath()` to support it flexibly.
bugOrRegression.author: lzhecheng
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix Windows credential provider cannot find binary. Windows credential provider binary path may have ".exe" suffix so it is better to use LookPath() to support it flexibly.

enrichment.problem: The Windows credential provider could not locate its binary because the lookup did not handle paths that include the ".exe" suffix, causing credential retrieval failures on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes that rely on the cloud provider credential provider (e.g., for accessing cloud APIs).
enrichment.fix: The code now uses Go's `LookPath()` to search for the credential provider binary, which correctly handles optional ".exe" extensions and finds the executable regardless of how the path is specified.

bugOrRegression.description: Added the `disable-force-detach` CLI option for `kube-controller-manager`. By default, it's set to `false`. When enabled, it prevents force detaching volumes based on maximum unmount time and node status. If activated, the non-graceful node shutdown feature must be used to recover from node failure. Additionally, if a pod needs to be forcibly terminated at the risk of corruption, the appropriate VolumeAttachment object must be deleted.
bugOrRegression.author: rohitssingh
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange:
This change adds the following CLI option for `kube-controller-manager`:
* `disable-force-detach` (defaults to `false`): Prevent force detaching volumes based on maximum unmount time and node status. If enabled, the non-graceful node shutdown feature must be used to recover from node failure (see https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/08/16/kubernetes-1-28-non-graceful-node-shutdown-ga/). If enabled and a pod must be forcibly terminated at the risk of corruption, then the appropriate VolumeAttachment object (see here: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/config-and-storage-resources/volume-attachment-v1/) must be deleted.

issueContext.title: Flag to Disable the 6-minute Force Detach Window
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Certain online upgrade workflows might need to restart kubernetes as a part of their upgrade procedure. This can lead to the following sequence:
* As a part of draining a kubernetes node, a pod might get deleted.
* The unmount of a pod could take more than 6 minutes.
* If the node is deemed unhealthy when the 6 minute timer fires for the pod being deleted (for example, because kubelet is still restarting), then the underlying PV will be force detached (via a `ControllerUnpublishVolume` RPC)

These workflows would likely benefit from disabling this feature in lieu of the Non-Graceful Node Shutdown feature that hit GA in kubernetes 1.28 (see [here](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/08/16/kubernetes-1-28-non-graceful-node-shutdown-ga/) for more details).

When these issues are encountered in our testbeds, we are left with Zombie iSCSI LUNs. If pods end up migrating to a node with such a Zombie LUN present, those pods might end up attaching themselves to the Zombie LUN leading to data corruption.

This data corruption has caused a number of our cluster-management applications to lose all access to their data, requiring them to be deployed from scratch (occasionally causing downtime for the entire cluster).

### What did you expect to happen?

The ControllerUnpublishVolume request to wait indefinitely until NodeUnstageVolume has succeeded.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See the “What happened?” section for more details.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
root@bootstrapper:~# kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"23", GitVersion:"v1.23.5", GitCommit:"c285e781331a3785a7f436042c65c5641ce8a9e9", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-03-16T15:58:47Z", GoVersion:"go1.17.8", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"27", GitVersion:"v1.27.4-gke.500", GitCommit:"a955253697d6572

enrichment.problem: During node upgrades or restarts, if a pod deletion takes longer than the default 6‑minute unmount window, the controller manager force‑detaches the underlying PersistentVolume. This can leave zombie iSCSI LUNs and cause data corruption when pods later attach to those stale volumes, leading to cluster‑wide data loss and downtime.
enrichment.affected: Clusters performing online upgrades or node restarts that use CSI‑backed PersistentVolumes (especially iSCSI). Pods that are deleted while unmounting could previously be force‑detached, leading to corrupted data.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `--disable-force-detach` flag (default false) to the kube‑controller‑manager. When enabled, the controller manager no longer force‑detaches volumes after the timeout. Administrators must instead use the non‑graceful node shutdown feature to recover from node failures, and manually delete the associated VolumeAttachment object if a pod must be force‑terminated.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental data corruption and zombie LUNs in upgrade or node‑restart scenarios, improving storage reliability for workloads that use CSI volumes (e.g., iSCSI). Gives operators explicit control over volume detach behavior, aligning with the GA non‑graceful node shutdown mechanism.

issueContext.title: Request timeout not respected while listing from storage
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

It is possible to issue a list request which exceeds the duration set by the request-timeout apiserver flag. The request-timeout flag does not appear to be enforced when the apiserver is decoding the response from etcd. 

Specifically, listing a large number of CRDs from etcd can result in high request latency from using json encoding compared to protobuf encoding. While overall etcd latency is low, the overall listing from storage latency may be over the 1 minute timeout, particularly if the apiserver needs to fetch multiple pages from etcd.



### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the list requests to be subject to the duration specified by the request-timeout flag when this latency is coming from the listing from storage phase of the request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create 4000 CRs and list all the objects from etcd in 2 pages of 2000 objects. If the time to list 1 page + decode takes around 50s, listing 2 pages will result in the listing from storage phase of the request taking  around 1 minute and 40s before the request fails and the client is returned a 500 response code.

Logs for apiserver Trace message:
```

```
Audit log entry:

  "kind": "Event",
  "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",
  "level":

enrichment.problem: When the API server decodes large etcd responses (e.g., listing thousands of CRDs), the decode step does not respect the request-timeout flag. This allows list requests to run longer than the configured timeout, ultimately returning a 500 error after the timeout period is exceeded.
enrichment.affected: Clients performing large list calls (e.g., CRD listings) against the API server; administrators configuring request-timeout expecting it to be enforced.
enrichment.fix: Update the etcd response decoding logic to honor the request’s timeout context, causing decoding to be cancelled when the timeout expires.
enrichment.impact: List operations that retrieve many objects will now be terminated according to the `--request-timeout` setting, preventing unexpectedly long latency and 500 errors. Improves reliability for clients performing large listings and ensures timeout semantics are consistent across the API server stack.

bugOrRegression.description: "Added `imagefs.inodesfree` to default `EvictionHard` settings."
bugOrRegression.author: vaibhav2107
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Add imagefs.inodesfree to default EvictionHard settings

issueContext.title: Default settings for EvictionHard do not include imagesfs.inodesFree.
issueContext.body:
It is possible to deploy Kubernetes with a separate filesystem.  We default the settings for EvictionHard [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blame/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/defaults_linux.go).

A concern is that if users are using the default settings and separate filesystem for images, we are effectively turning off monitoring for INodes on the imagefs.  This means that we won't have disk pressure if inodes run out on the ImageFs.  

The fix can be to add 

```
var DefaultEvictionHard = map[string]string{
	"memory.available":  "100Mi",
	"nodefs.available":  "10%",
	"nodefs.inodesFree": "5%",
	"imagefs.available": "15%",
        "imagefs.inodesFree": "5%",
}
```
To default settings.

This doesn't seem to be a regression as these defaults were added 5 years ago (k8s 1.12) but this could be a potential bug if either users mount a separate filesystem to their container runtime storage or they configure their runtime to store their images on a separate filesystem.

enrichment.problem: The default EvictionHard thresholds did not include monitoring of free inodes on the image filesystem (imagefs), so nodes using a separate imagefs could run out of inodes without triggering disk pressure eviction.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where the container runtime stores images on a separate filesystem (imagefs) and relies on default eviction settings.
enrichment.fix: Added "imagefs.inodesFree": "5%" to the kubelet's DefaultEvictionHard map, ensuring inode pressure on imagefs is considered for eviction decisions.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that store container images on a dedicated filesystem will now evict pods when inode usage exceeds the threshold, preventing node instability or failures caused by exhausted inodes.

issueContext.title: No proper scheduling retries could be made when Extender filters out some Nodes
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When Extender filters out some Nodes, we don't set any unschedulable plugins at all. It means Extender is completely ignored during the requeueing process.

So, what's happening is:
- If Extender filters out all Nodes during scheduling, this Pod is soon retried because this Pod doesn't have any plugin name in unschedulable plugins.
- If Extender filters out some Nodes during scheduling and plugins filter out all other Nodes, this Pod is retried based on plugins' QueueingHint. Even if any cluster events happen and it could change Extender's decision (but not any plugins' decision), this Pod won't be requeued to activeQ/backoffQ.

The latter case is serious because it could make Pods being stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min.

### What did you expect to happen?

We should have a short-term solution for the latter case. 
We can requeue Pods, which were rejected by Extender, by any kind of cluster events because we cannot know which events make Pods schedulable.

Eventually, this issue makes us wonder how Pods rejected by Extender should be requeued. We cannot implement QHint equivalent in Extenders because it'd be too slow to call Extender every time any cluster events happen. Probably, somehow implementing EventsToRegister equivalent in Extender? 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use Extender which does something in Filter.

issueContext.title: Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled:
```
E1127 19:48:13.221979   66549 schedule_one.go:130] "Error selecting node for pod" err="applying score defaultWeights on Score plugins: plugin \"PodTopologySpread\" returns an invalid score 300, it should in the range of [0, 100] after normalizing" pod="default/test-multi-point-xxxxxxxx"
```

After investigation, I found that there was a bug in the code that built the framework when the scheduler started. When using the plugins declared in the regular extension point to override the plugins declared in the MultiPoint, the traversed variable `enabledSet` will be modified in the following loop:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad9b60e2c9ddb21e8b00cabbe27e639638a0ea88/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L523-L534

This may cause **a same scoring plugin** (e.g. `PodTopologySpread`) **to be loaded multiple times**:
```
f.scorePlugins: []framework.ScorePlugin{(*noderesources.Fit)(0xc000922e10), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*tainttoleration.TaintToleration)(0xc0003f3690), (*nodeaffinity.NodeAffinity)(0xc0003997a0), (*volumebinding.VolumeBinding)(0xc0003db7a0), (*interpodaffinity.InterPodAffinity)(0xc00038f3b0), (*noderesources.BalancedAllocation)(0xc000063680), (*imagelocality.ImageLocality)(0xc000b45320)}
```

Further, this results in **a node being processed multiple times by a plugin's** (e.g. `PodTopologySpread`'s) **`NormalizeScore` method**, resulting in an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100]:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad9b60e2c9ddb21e8b00cabbe27e639638a0ea88/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L1095-L1108

### What did you expect to happen?

If the scheduler's MultiPoint feature is used (either through the default plugins or through manual configuration),

enrichment.problem: When overriding MultiPoint plugins (e.g., default scheduler plugins) the framework loop mutated the enabledSet, causing the same scoring plugin to be registered multiple times. This produced invalid scores (outside 0‑100) and prevented any pod from being scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that customize the scheduler by overriding default MultiPoint plugins (e.g., using custom scheduler profiles) were affected because the duplicated plugin caused all pods to be unschedulable.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the plugin registration loop in pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go to preserve the original enabledSet and avoid loading a plugin more than once when MultiPoint plugins are overridden.
enrichment.impact: Restores normal scheduling behavior; pods are no longer blocked by duplicate plugin instances and invalid scores, allowing clusters to schedule workloads as expected.

issueContext.title: endpoints not configured with MinimizeIPTablesRestore
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

To test out the MinimizeIPTablesRestore feature enabled in 1.27 by default we enabled the setting in 1.26 and discovered that it appears to not configure endpoints properly everytime.
While the version in 1.26 is still alpha I have not found any significant changes, bug reports or backports in the changelog regarding this.

It seems sometimes kube-proxy does not see that the endpoints of a service need to be updated despite the api endpointslice having changed. This typically is not that visible with externalTrafficPolicy Cluster services as some other endpoint still is configured, but in the case of low replica services or externalTrafficPolicy Local services this can lead to service disruption due to the only endpoint on the local node not getting configured while other components see the update correctly and direct traffic there.


For example this two pod deployment both pods ready since hours:

--

      status: "True"
      type: Ready
--
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:20:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: ContainersReady

```

and the chain on one node only contains one of the ready endpoints:

```

KUBE-SVC-APW7J2FZSA

enrichment.problem: A race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy could cause endpoint updates to be lost, meaning new service endpoints were not added to iptables rules promptly. This resulted in traffic routing failures, especially for low‑replica services or services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy in iptables mode (default from v1.27) where services have changing endpoints, particularly low‑replica or externalTrafficPolicy=Local services.

bugOrRegression.description: Reverted the `QueueingHint` implementation for `NodeUnschedulable` due to potential scenarios where events that make Pods schedulable could be missed.

bugOrRegression.description: Improved the efficiency of NodeAdded QueueingHint by registering UpdateNodeTaint event for plugins that have NodeAdded event but don't have UpdateNodeTaint event. This ensures better requeuing efficiency and prevents Pods from being stuck in the unschedulable pod pool.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange:
Currently, NodeAdded QueueingHint could not always be called because of the internal feature called preCheck.
It's definitely not something expected for plugin developers,
and we're trying to eventually remove preCheck completely to fix this.
Until then we'll register UpdateNodeTaint event for plugins that have NodeAdded event, but don't have UpdateNodeTaint event.
It'd result in a bad impact on the requeuing efficiency though, a lot better than some Pods being stuck in the
unschedulable pod pool.

issueContext.title: plugins that register nodeAdd in EventsToRegister must register nodeUpdate
issueContext.body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

Plugins may miss Node-related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

So, no matter whether plugins have QueueingHint or not, plugins must register NodeUpdate event when they're interested in NodeAdd. Also, in case they have QHint, they should take this scenario into consideration.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's NodeAdded QueueingHint is sometimes skipped because the internal preCheck filters out the NodeAdded event. Plugins that only register the NodeAdded event miss the subsequent NodeUpdate event, causing pods to remain in the unschedulable pod pool.
enrichment.affected: Scheduler plugins that rely on NodeAdded events without also handling NodeUpdate, and the workloads (pods) that were left unschedulable.
enrichment.fix: For plugins that declare a NodeAdded event but not an UpdateNodeTaint (NodeUpdate) event, the scheduler now automatically registers the UpdateNodeTaint event. This ensures the plugin receives a node update when the node becomes ready, improving requeue efficiency and preventing pods from being stuck.
enrichment.impact: Pods that were previously unable to be scheduled after a node becomes ready will now be re‑queued promptly, reducing scheduling delays and improving overall cluster throughput.

issueContext.title: Scheduler evaluates many nodes even if there are no scoring plugins defined
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Even when no scoring plugins are defined, scheduler always attempts to find multiple nodes where the pod can run. This is unnecessary (and therefore inefficient) when we know ahead of time that there will be no difference between how those nodes are scored. 

### What did you expect to happen?

If we're going to pick a random node, we can just as well cut short the search after finding the first match.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure scheduler without any scoring plugins and see that mulitple nodes are evaluated anyway.

### Anything else we need to know?

/cc @ahg-g @alculquicondor 
/sig scheduling
/kind bug

### Kubernetes version

1.29 and older

### Cloud provider

N/A

### OS version

_No response_

### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the default kube-scheduler with a configuration that omits all scoring plugins; pods that are placed using random node selection.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now stops searching after the first feasible node is found if there are no scoring plugins defined, eliminating the extra node evaluations.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling latency is reduced and CPU consumption is lowered, especially in large clusters or in scenarios where scoring plugins are disabled.
