issueContext.title: False MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failure warning message for readOnly pods
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Created a RWX volume and mounted it on a pod having readOnly flag set to true.

While the volume provisioning happened successfully, we did observe some warning message on describing the pod:

`Warning  FileSystemResizeFailed  27m   kubelet                  MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failed for volume "pvc-d766a8a5-a6ba-49f4-a560-0c5e15b4ab74" requested read-only file system
 `

It seems like this message is being triggered from here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L2079


But we never did an expand volume call, so we should not be seeing warning message. It can be confusing to see this warning message.

### What did you expect to happen?

The warning message should not be displayed when expand volume was not even called.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a RWX volume and mount it on a pod with readOnly flag set to true. Wait for a few minutes and describe the pod.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.28

### Cloud provider

vSphere

### OS version

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>

enrichment.problem: Kubelet emitted a warning event `FileSystemResizeFailed` when creating a pod that used a readOnly volume, even though no volume expansion was performed and the volume's capacity met or exceeded the requested storage. This false warning could mislead users into thinking a resize had failed.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that mounts a volume with `readOnly: true` where the volume's capacity is greater than or equal to the requested storage, typically RWX volumes. The false warning appeared in `kubectl describe pod` output.
enrichment.fix: The code path that generated the `FileSystemResizeFailed` event for readOnly volumes with sufficient capacity has been removed, so the warning is no longer emitted in this scenario.
enrichment.impact: Users no longer see confusing warning events for readOnly pods, reducing noise in pod descriptions and preventing unnecessary troubleshooting for a non‑issue.

bugOrRegression.description: "kubeadm: Added better handling of errors during unmount when calling `kubeadm reset`. In such situations, it is better for you to inspect the problem and resolve it manually. Then, you can call `kubeadm reset` again to complete the cleanup."

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kubeadm: add better handling of errors during unmount when calling "kubeadm reset". When failing to unmount directories under "/var/run/kubelet", kubeadm will now throw an error instead of showing a warning and continuing to cleanup said directory. In such situations it is better for you to inspect the problem and resolve it manually, then you can call "kubeadm reset" again to complete the cleanup.

enrichment.problem: When running `kubeadm reset`, failures to unmount directories under `/var/run/kubelet` were only logged as warnings and the reset continued, leaving potentially stale mounts and incomplete cleanup without alerting the user.

bugOrRegression.description: "Changed the API server so that for admission webhooks that have a URL matching the hostname 'localhost' or a loopback IP address, the connection supports HTTP/2 where it could be negotiated."

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Changed the API server so that for admission webhooks that have a URL matching the hostname `localhost`, or a loopback IP address, the connection supports HTTP/2 where it can be negotiated.

enrichment.problem: Admission webhook calls that target a service on localhost or a loopback IP were forced to use HTTP/1.1, preventing the use of HTTP/2 even when the webhook server supported it, which could cause unnecessary latency and higher CPU usage.

enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver now negotiates HTTP/2 for admission webhook connections whose URL resolves to "localhost" or a loopback IP address, falling back to HTTP/1.1 only when HTTP/2 cannot be negotiated.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where `kubectl` drain would consider a pod as having been deleted if an error occurs while calling the API.

bugOrRegression.description: The PersistentVolume controller no longer automatically assigns a default `StorageClass` to Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) with an empty `storageClassName`.

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fixes a regression in 1.26+ default configurations: If a pvc has an empty storageClassName, persistentvolume controller won't try to assign a default StorageClass

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.26+, PVCs that explicitly set `storageClassName: ""` (empty string) were mistakenly assigned the cluster's default StorageClass by the PersistentVolume controller, contrary to the intended behavior of having no storage class.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a regression in "kubeadm init" where a user-specified --kubeconfig file was being ignored.

issueContext.title: Aggregated Discovery doesn't show aggregated apiservices as Stale before initial health check
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

[Quote from KEP 3352](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/3352-aggregated-discovery#aggregation):

> A post start hook will be added and the kube-apiserver health check should only pass if the discovery document is ready. Since aggregated api servers may take longer to respond and we do not want to delay cluster startup, the health check will only block on the local api servers (built-ins and CRDs) to have their discovery ready. For api servers that have not been aggregated, their group-versions will be published with an empty resource list and a Stale for Freshness to indicate that they have not synced yet.

This requirement is not met. Explanation in first comment shows we wait for local services to sync before health check, but we do not include aggregated apiservices that had not yet synced as Stale.

/cc @Jefftree @apelisse 
/sig api-machinery

### What did you expect to happen?

Unsynced aggregated APIServices which appear in the initial list for apiserver are included in document before health check with empty resource list and `Stale` freshness.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

N/A

issueContext.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy using CRDs as paramKind always fails after restarting kube-apiserver
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I'm using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy(VAP) with setting my own CRD to paramKind in my on-premise cluster. It works fine, but once I restarted one of the kube-apiserver instances it changed to reject both valid and invalid requests with the error message like:

```
error: failed to create rolebinding: rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "view" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'test-vap' denied request: failed to configure policy: failed to find resource referenced by paramKind: 'example.com/v1alpha1, Kind=Foo'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

VAP using CRDs as paramKind should continue to work fine even when one of kube-apiserver instances is restarted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can reproduce it locally using kind cluster by following procedure.

<details>

```
$ cat kind.yaml         
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
  kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: ClusterConfiguration
    apiServer:
      extraArgs:
        feature-gates: "ValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true"
        runtime-config: "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1=true"

$ kind create cluster --image=kindest/node:v1.29.0 --config kind.yaml
Creating cluster "kind" ...
 ✓ Ensuring node image (kindest/node:v1.29.0) 🖼
 ✓ Preparing nodes 📦  
 ✓ Writing configuration 📜 
 ✓ Starting control-plane 🕹️ 
 ✓ Installing CNI 🔌 
 ✓ Installing StorageClass 💾 
Set kubectl context to "kind-kind"
You can now use your cluster with:
kubectl cluster-info --context kind-kind
Thanks for using kind! 😊

$ cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -                                                                  
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: foos.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: Foo
    listKind: FooList
    plural: foos
    singular: foo
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - nam

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects that used a CustomResourceDefinition as paramKind stopped synchronizing after a kube-apiserver restart, causing the policy to deny all requests (both valid and invalid) with errors like "failed to find resource referenced by paramKind".

enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on VAPs with CRD parameters can now restart the API server without breaking admission checks, restoring normal request processing and preventing accidental denial of legitimate operations.

issueContext.title: sidecar container readniess result to be used in Pod ready state also for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Never or OnFailure
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I created a pod with sidecar container with following manifest:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: simple-webapp
  labels:
    app: webapp
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "key1"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  initContainers:
    - name: init-service
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 5s
    - name: sidecar
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 30s
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-logs
          mountPath: /var/log/nginx
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
          - cat
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 5
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main-application
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
      - name: shared-logs
        mountPath: /var/log/nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "100Mi"
        cpu: "0.5"
  volumes:
    - name: shared-logs
      emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never

```

watch the pod readiness. 
```
#before the sidecar container be restarted , the readiness is 2/2
watch kubectl  get pod
Every 2.0s: kubectl get pod                                                     

NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           2/2     Running   0          36s

#after the sidecar container be restarted, the pod readiness is 1/2, sidecar readiness result is not be used to the pod. 
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           1/2     Running   2          2m15s

```
in [Sidecar containers and Pod lifecycle](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/#sidecar-containers-and-pod-lifecycle), it's mentioned "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod."

it's true only for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Always, sidecar

enrichment.problem: An init (or sidecar) container that has `restartPolicy: Always` could not transition its state from terminated back to running when the pod’s `restartPolicy` was set to `Never` or `OnFailure`. As a result the pod’s overall readiness status was not updated after the container restarted, causing stale readiness information.
enrichment.affected: Users running Pods with init or sidecar containers that set `restartPolicy: Always` while the pod itself uses `restartPolicy: Never` or `OnFailure`. The issue manifested as readiness counts dropping and not recovering after the sidecar container restarted.
enrichment.fix: Implemented logic to allow containers with `containerRestartPolicy: Always` to update their state from terminated to non‑terminated even when the pod’s `restartPolicy` is `Never` or `OnFailure`, ensuring the pod status reflects the current container state.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on always‑restarting init/sidecar containers (e.g., for log collection, readiness gating, or auxiliary tasks) now correctly report readiness after a container restart. This prevents false‑positive readiness and improves reliability of workload health checks.

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Even when no scoring plugins are defined, scheduler always attempts to find multiple nodes where the pod can run. This is unnecessary (and therefore inefficient) when we know ahead of time that there will be no difference between how those nodes are scored. 

### What did you expect to happen?

If we're going to pick a random node, we can just as well cut short the search after finding the first match.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure scheduler without any scoring plugins and see that mulitple nodes are evaluated anyway.

1.29 and older

_No response_

_No response_

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-scheduler with scoring plugins disabled; pods that are scheduled without any scoring criteria are affected.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now short‑circuits the node search when there are no scoring plugins, selecting the first feasible node and skipping further evaluations.

### What happened?

When installing the metrics-server to implement the metrics.k8s.io API and the prometheus-adapter to implement the custom.metrics.k8s.io API, it is possible to make the OpenAPI handler fail to initialize with this error log in apiserver: https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/blob/master/pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go#L343

handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/{namespace}/pods
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes/{name}

This will result in kubectl discovery calls to /openapi/v2 to fail with a 503:

...

The OpenAPI handler should not fail to initialize if both metrics.k8s.io and custom.metrics.k8s.io are serving the same path for different API groups/versions.

### How can we rep

enrichment.problem: The OpenAPI v2 endpoint merged aggregated API server specs for group-versions that did not match the APIService’s declared group version, causing duplicate paths (e.g., metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1) and making the OpenAPI handler fail to initialize, resulting in 503 errors on /openapi/v2 discovery calls.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run aggregated API servers with overlapping group versions (such as metrics.k8s.io) and any tooling that relies on the OpenAPI v2 discovery endpoint.
enrichment.fix: The change restricts OpenAPI v2 publishing to only those aggregated API server group-versions that exactly match the APIService’s specified group version, preventing duplicate path merges and allowing the OpenAPI handler to start successfully.
enrichment.impact: Restores successful /openapi/v2 discovery for clusters using multiple aggregated APIs (e.g., metrics-server and prometheus-adapter), preventing kubectl and other clients from encountering 503 errors and ensuring API discovery continues to work.

bugOrRegression.description: [kubeadam][structured authz] avoided setting default `--authorization-mode` when `--authorization-config` is provided

issueContext.title: [kubeadam][structured authz] can't use structured authz due to default `--authorization-mode` flag
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

**TL;DR**
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L232 prevents us from using structured authz (setting `--authorization-config` flag) as those flags are mutually exclusive

/cc @palnabarun (as the author of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120154)
/cc @liggitt 

FYI @stealthybox @robscott 

To use structured authz you need to define the authorization configuration using the `--authorization-config` flag.

However this flag is mutually exclusive with `--authorization-modes` and `--authorization-webhook-*` flags.  (refer to [1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authorization.go#L113) & [2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authorization/#configuring-the-api-server-using-an-authorization-config-file))

Kubeadam adds `--authorization-mode` by default ([1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L232) & [2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c11cc9cfcdc54a7ca4efdc10609bf421bfa54d4/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/controlplane/manifests.go#L241)) which prevents us from using `--authorization-config`

### What did you expect to happen?

I should be able to define the `authorization-config`  flag and have structured authz working.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Spin up a kind cluster using this kind config (make sure the images are > 1.29 for structured authz to be avaliable)

```yaml
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
featureGates:
  StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration: true
kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: ClusterConfiguration
    metadata:
      name: config
    apiServer:
      extraArgs:
        authorization-config: "/files/authorization_config.yaml" 
      e

enrichment.problem: kubeadm always adds the default `--authorization-mode` flag even when a user provides `--authorization-config`. Since these flags are mutually exclusive, the API server fails to start, preventing the use of structured authorization.
enrichment.affected: Users who bootstrap a control‑plane with kubeadm and want to configure the API server via `--authorization-config` (structured authz). The API server would previously refuse to start due to conflicting flags.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now skips setting the default `--authorization-mode` flag when `--authorization-config` is specified, allowing the API server to use the provided authorization configuration file.
enrichment.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm can now enable structured authorization without manual manifest edits, simplifying secure authorization configuration and avoiding API server startup failures.

bugOrRegression.description: "Fixed a non-recursive list returning "resource version too high" error when consistent listing from cache is enabled."

bugOrRegression.description: The initialization of nodes using external cloud providers now waits for the providerID value to be available before untainting it. This ensures that nodes are not declared Ready without necessary information such as the providerID and zone labels, which are required for integrations like load balancers to function correctly. Cloud providers that do not implement the GetInstanceProviderID method will not require the providerID to be set and will not fail to initialize the node for backward compatibility.
bugOrRegression.author: aojea
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: The initialization of nodes using external cloud-providers now waits for the providerID value to be available before untainting it. This is required because , if there are communication errors with the cloud-provider on the cloud-controller-manager, nodes may have been declared Ready without having this field or the zone labels, and this information was never reconciled. The providerID and the zone labels are required for integrations like loadbalancers to work correctly. Cloud providers that does not implement the `GetInstanceProviderID` method will not require the providerID to be set and will not fail to initialize the node for backward compatibility issues.

enrichment.problem: Nodes using external cloud providers could be marked Ready before the providerID and zone labels were set due to communication errors with the cloud-controller-manager, causing integrations like load balancers to malfunction.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use external cloud providers (e.g., AWS, GCE, Azure) where the cloud‑controller‑manager may experience communication issues, affecting node readiness and cloud‑specific features.
enrichment.fix: Node initialization now waits for the providerID to become available before removing the node's NoSchedule taint, ensuring the providerID and zone labels are present. Providers that do not implement GetInstanceProviderID retain backward compatibility and are not required to set providerID.
enrichment.impact: Prevents nodes from becoming Ready without essential cloud metadata, ensuring load balancer and other cloud‑provider integrations work correctly and improving overall cluster reliability.

issueContext.title: DRA API: don't allow changing object meta during status update
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The strategy.go's `PrepareForStatusUpdate` was copied from some other, broken types. A call to `ResetObjectMetaForStatus` is missing and therefore, for example, finalizers can be changed during a status update. That is not supposed to be possible.

### What did you expect to happen?

Object meta changes need to be removed during status updates.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

n/a

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Since 1.26 till at least 1.29.

### Cloud provider

n/a

### OS version

_No response_

### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

enrichment.problem: During status subresource updates for DRA objects (ResourceClaim and PodSchedulingContext), object metadata such as finalizers could be modified because PrepareForStatusUpdate omitted a call to ResetObjectMetaForStatus, violating API semantics.
enrichment.affected: Users and controllers that create or manage Device Resource Allocation (DRA) objects, specifically ResourceClaim and PodSchedulingContext resources.
enrichment.fix: The status update handling was corrected to reset object metadata, disallowing any changes to object meta (e.g., finalizers) when only the status field is being updated.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unintended metadata changes that could corrupt object lifecycle (e.g., finalizer handling), ensuring DRA API behavior is consistent and reliable for controllers and workloads that use ResourceClaim and PodSchedulingContext.

bugOrRegression.description: kube-apiserver: Fixed a `1.27`+ regression in watch stability by serving watch requests without a `resourceVersion` from the watch cache by default, as in <`1.27` (disabling the change in PR 115096 by default). This mitigates the impact of an etcd watch bug (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/17555). If the 1.27 change in PR 115096 to serve these requests from underlying storage is still desired despite the impact on watch stability, it can be re-enabled with a `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression in watch stability by serving watch requests without a resourceVersion from the watch cache by default, as in <1.27 (disabling the change in #115096 by default). This mitigates the impact of an etcd watch bug (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/17555). If the 1.27 change in #115096 to serve these requests from underlying storage is still desired despite the impact on watch stability, it can be re-enabled with a `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.

enrichment.problem: Starting in Kubernetes 1.27, a change (PR #115096) made the apiserver serve watch requests without a resourceVersion directly from storage. Combined with an etcd watch bug, this caused unstable watch streams, leading to missed events and broken controllers.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or controller that relies on watch APIs (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, custom operators) experienced instability after upgrading to 1.27+.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now defaults to serving watch requests without a resourceVersion from the watch cache (the pre‑1.27 behavior), disabling the PR #115096 change. Users can still enable the storage‑based behavior via the `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate if desired.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable watch behavior for all clients and controllers, preventing watch disconnects and ensuring correct event delivery. This mitigates the downstream impact of the etcd watch bug.

feature.author: sanposhiho

issueContext.title: Request timeout not respected while listing from storage
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

It is possible to issue a list request which exceeds the duration set by the request-timeout apiserver flag. The request-timeout flag does not appear to be enforced when the apiserver is decoding the response from etcd. 

Specifically, listing a large number of CRDs from etcd can result in high request latency from using json encoding compared to protobuf encoding. While overall etcd latency is low, the overall listing from storage latency may be over the 1 minute timeout, particularly if the apiserver needs to fetch multiple pages from etcd.



### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the list requests to be subject to the duration specified by the request-timeout flag when this latency is coming from the listing from storage phase of the request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create 4000 CRs and list all the objects from etcd in 2 pages of 2000 objects. If the time to list 1 page + decode takes around 50s, listing 2 pages will result in the listing from storage phase of the request taking  around 1 minute and 40s before the request fails and the client is returned a 500 response code.

Logs for apiserver Trace message:
```
I0918 10:52:29.592390      11 trace.go:205] Trace[474507988]: "List(recursive=true) etcd3" key:/<key>,resourceVersion:,resourceVersionMatch:,limit:0,continue: (18-Sep-2023 10:50:47.716) (total time: 101875ms):
Trace[474507988]: ---"fetched all pages from etcd" page-count:2 101875ms (10:52:29.592)
Trace[474507988]: [1m41.875605715s] [1m41.875605715s] END

I0918 10:52:29.596639      11 trace.go:205] Trace[1368262150]: "List" url:/apis/<CRD-path>,user-agent:<user>,audit-id:c3badffb-7382-468e-9669-caadf5c85fc1,client:<IP>,accept:application/json,protocol:HTTP/2.0 (18-Sep-2023 10:50:47.716) (total time: 101880ms):
Trace[1368262150]: [1m41.880102098s] [1m41.880102098s] END
```
Audit log entry:
```
{
  "kind": "Event",
  "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",
  "level":

enrichment.problem: The apiserver's request-timeout flag is not enforced during the storage listing phase because decoding large response objects (e.g., many CRDs) can take significant time, causing requests to exceed the timeout without being aborted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that perform large list operations (e.g., thousands of CRDs) and rely on the request-timeout flag; also operators using audit logs for debugging.
enrichment.fix: Added the `apiserver.latency.k8s.io/decode-response-object` annotation to audit logs, recording the time spent decoding response objects. This provides visibility into decoding latency for troubleshooting and future improvements.
enrichment.impact: Admins can now see how much time is spent decoding responses, identify latency issues that bypass request-timeout enforcement, and take corrective actions (e.g., switch to protobuf, tune request sizes). Improves observability and aids in preventing long‑running list operations from silently exceeding timeout limits.

feature.author: liggitt

issueContext.title: [StructuredAuthorizationConfig] Implement reloading of configuration
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Implement reloading of configuration in a loop at defined time intervals.

- Replace active authorizer on successful load and validation pass.
- Log and metric on failure

From the KEP:
The API server will periodically reload the configuration at a specific time interval. If it or any of referenced files change, and the new configuration passes validation, then the new configuration will be used for the Authorizer chain. The reloader will also check if the webhook is healthy, thereby preventing any typo/misconfiguration with the Webhook resulting in bad Authorizer config. If healthcheck on the webhook failed, the last known good config will be used. In the next iteration of reload, if webhook is found to be healthy, the new config will be used. Logging and metrics would be used to signal success/failure of a config reload so that cluster admins can have observability over this process. Reload must not add or remove Node or RBAC authorizers. They can be reordered, but cannot be added or removed.



### Why is this needed?

Implements https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3221-structured-authorization-configuration

enrichment.problem: Changes to the --authorization-config file required a full kube-apiserver restart to take effect, forcing administrators to reload the API server to update authorization policies.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the --authorization-config flag for structured authorization. Administrators updating auth policies benefit from automatic reloads; API server workloads remain uninterrupted during reload attempts.
enrichment.fix: kube-apiserver now watches the --authorization-config file and automatically reloads it when the file changes. Successful reloads replace the active authorizer, emit a success metric (status="success"), and failed reloads emit a failure metric (status="failed") while continuing to use the previously loaded configuration.
enrichment.impact: Admins can update structured authorization configuration without downtime, improving operational agility and reducing service disruption. The added metrics provide visibility into reload success or failure, aiding troubleshooting and observability.

issueContext.title: cronjob controller: reconsider log verbosity
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We are running Kubernetes 1.25.5 and trying to configure kube-controller-manager to be less verbose when logging.
We run kube-controller-manager as a static pod created by Kubelet and use the following command where we pass `--v=0`:
```
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
    - kube-controller-manager
    - --feature-gates=EphemeralContainers=true,TopologyAwareHints=true
    - --allocate-node-cidrs=true
    - --authentication-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --authorization-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --cluster-cidr=10.6.0.0/16
    - --configure-cloud-routes=false
    - --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf
    - --leader-elect=true
    - --node-monitor-grace-period=120s
    - --root-ca-file=/etc/kubernetes/ssl/ca.pem
    - --service-account-private-key-file=/etc/kubernetes/ssl/signing-key.pem
    - --use-service-account-credentials
    - --v=0
    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.25.5
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    livenessProbe:
      failureThreshold: 3
      httpGet:
        host: 127.0.0.1
        path: /healthz
        port: 10257
        scheme: HTTPS
      initialDelaySeconds: 15
      periodSeconds: 10
      successThreshold: 1
      timeoutSeconds: 15
    name: kube-controller-manager
```
The `--v=0` flag seems to passed fine to the final command line of kube-controller-manager:
```
root     2464651  285  1.6 1939088 1085624 ?     Ssl  05:59 544:37 kube-controller-manager --feature-gates=EphemeralContainers=true,TopologyAwareHints=true --allocate-node-cidrs=true --authentication-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf --authorization-kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf --cluster-cidr=10.6.0.0/16 --configure-cloud-routes=false --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/config/controller-manager.conf --leader-elect=true --node-monitor-grace-period=120s --root-ca-file=/

enrichment.problem: Even when users set a low global verbosity (e.g., --v=0) for kube-controller-manager, the event broadcaster still logs messages at a higher verbosity, causing noisy logs that cannot be suppressed.
enrichment.affected: Operators running kube-controller-manager who want low‑verbosity logs; any deployment where log noise from event messages obscures important information.
enrichment.fix: The global logging level for the broadcaster is raised to 3. With this default, lowering the controller‑manager's log level (e.g., to 0) now suppresses event messages, reducing unnecessary output.
enrichment.impact: Clusters see cleaner controller‑manager logs, making it easier for operators to spot real issues and reducing log storage/processing overhead.

feature.author: Gekko0114
feature.userFacingChange: Allow scheduling framework plugins that implement io.Closer to be gracefully closed.

issueContext.title: Allow framework plugins to be closed
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like `framework.Plugin` implementations, specifically scheduler plugins to be when the scheduler is being stopped. It could implement this by a type assertion on `io.Closer`, so that old schedulers don't have to implement it.

### Why is this needed?

For example, wasm plugins internally use mapped memory and it would be good to cleanly unmap them.

Without this we could use finalizers, but doing that has problems including [some overhead](https://lemire.me/blog/2023/05/19/the-absurd-cost-of-finalizers-in-go/).

enrichment.problem: Scheduler plugins could not be cleanly shut down, causing resource leaks (e.g., wasm plugins with mapped memory) and requiring costly finalizers.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running custom scheduler plugins that implement io.Closer (e.g., wasm plugins). Existing plugins without Close() are unaffected.
enrichment.fix: During kube-scheduler shutdown, the framework now detects plugins that implement io.Closer and invokes their Close() method, allowing graceful cleanup of plugin resources.

feature.description: Scheduler extender `ignorable` option now handles errors for both filter and bind phases.
feature.author: sunbinnnnn
feature.userFacingChange: The option `ignorable` of scheduler extender can skip error both filter and bind.

issueContext.title: kube-scheduler extender.IsIgnorable() is not work for bind path
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

I use extenders to add webhook for default-scheduler:
```
extenders:
- enableHTTPS: false
  filterVerb: filter
  bindVerb: bind
  weight: 1
  httpTimeout: 0s
  nodeCacheCapable: true
  ignorable: true
  urlPrefix: http://10.108.198.121:9040/v1
```
And set `ignorable: true` to ignore scheuler error when scheduler extender is not working.
But I got an error: `Post "http://10.108.198.121:9040/v1/bind": dial tcp 10.108.198.121:9040: connect: connection timed out`.

I suppose  `ignorable` work fine in predicate path, but not work fine in bind path.

The Ignorable logic in kube-scheduler:
_pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go: 637:_
```go
...
		feasibleList, failedMap, failedAndUnresolvableMap, err := extender.Filter(pod, feasibleNodes)
		if err != nil {
			if extender.IsIgnorable() {
				logger.Info("Skipping extender as it returned error and has ignorable flag set", "extender", extender, "err", err)
				continue
			}
			return nil, err
		}
...
```
and,
_pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go: 905:_
```go
...
func (sched *Scheduler) extendersBinding(pod *v1.Pod, node string) (bool, error) {
	for _, extender := range sched.Extenders {
		if !extender.IsBinder() || !extender.IsInterested(pod) {
			continue
		}
		return true, extender.Bind(&v1.Binding{
			ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Namespace: pod.Namespace, Name: pod.Name, UID: pod.UID},
			Target:     v1.ObjectReference{Kind: "Node", Name: node},
		})
	}
	return false, nil
}
...
```
the `ignorable` is not judge in `extendersBinding`.


### What did you expect to happen?

Schedule should not error when set `ignorable=true`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.add extenders to kube-scheduler config(which has filterVerb and bindVerb and ignorable flag), example:
```
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration
leaderElection:
  leaderElect: true
  leaseDuration: 0s
  renewDeadline: 0s

enrichment.problem: When `ignorable: true` was set on a scheduler extender, errors in the bind phase were not ignored, causing pod scheduling to fail if the extender's bind endpoint was unreachable.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on a scheduler extender with `ignorable: true`, especially when the extender's bind service is unavailable or slow.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now checks the extender's `IsIgnorable()` flag during both filter and bind phases. If an error occurs in the bind call and the extender is marked ignorable, the failure is logged and the scheduler proceeds without aborting the schedule.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using extenders with `ignorable: true` no longer experience pod scheduling failures due to temporary extender bind errors, improving reliability and resilience of custom scheduling workflows.

issueContext.title: Metric process_start_time_seconds is not defined for /metrics/slis
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

/metrics/slis was added for several components (apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, cloud-controller-manager) in https://kep.k8s.io/3466

This is to propose adding metric `process_start_time_seconds` to these components  for /metrics/slis to support cumulative metric `kubernetes_healthchecks_total`

### Why is this needed?

Missing start time metric in metrics/slis will result in inaccurate cumulative metrics.

Even though the start time metric is available in /metrics, it requires the metrics collector to scrape two endpoints at once and sync them to prepare the cumulative metric data.

enrichment.problem: The /metrics/slis endpoint for core control-plane components did not expose the process_start_time_seconds metric, preventing accurate calculation of the cumulative kubernetes_healthchecks_total metric and forcing collectors to scrape both /metrics and /metrics/slis.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that expose the /metrics/slis endpoint – API server, controller manager, scheduler, kubelet, and cloud controller manager – as well as any monitoring setups that rely on these metrics.
enrichment.fix: Added the process_start_time_seconds metric to the /metrics/slis endpoint of all components (apiserver, controller‑manager, scheduler, kubelet, cloud‑controller‑manager).
enrichment.impact: Monitoring systems can now derive accurate health‑check totals from a single scrape, simplifying metric collection and improving observability of component start times.

issueContext.title: Scheduler:  Share `frameworkImpl.waitingPods` among profiles
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

I hope to share the `waitingPods` among multiple profiles, instead of creating a new `waitingPods` in each profiles with the current implementation.

In other words, `waitingPods` is only instantiated once in a scheduler app.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1ffdedf782edf1472102b0b99c1467d4ed39753/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L253-L258


@Huang-Wei @ahg-g  PTAL, Is there any negative impact of this change that I didn't consider, thanks.

### Why is this needed?

In some scenarios, I need to traverse `all pods` waiting in the permit stage within the current scheduler app, rather than the pods that using the current profile for scheduling and waiting in the permit stage.

For example, we want use [coscheduling](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins/blob/master/pkg/coscheduling/README.md) to achieve `all-or-nothing`. And we have abstracted the concept of a `Cluster`, where there are two deployments under each cluster. Each deployments use different scheduler profile, and one cluster corresponds to one podGroup, as following:
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/18323315/256ffd20-6adc-4dc5-b249-d6ffcafed303)

Then, we want pods in one cluster (podA1, podA2, podB1) to be scheduled succeed/failed together. 

We assume that all pods can pass through the filter plugins, and `podA2` is the last to be scheduled. At this point, `podA1` and `podB1` are both waiting in the permit stage. Afterwards, we traverse the `waitingPods` to complete the permit waiting for `podA1` and `podB1`. However, from an implementation perspective, now we can only see `podA1` in `waitingPods`, `podB1` cannot be seen, because`podA2` & `podB1` use different scheduling profiles. Which will cause `podB1` timeout during the permit phase, even if all pods within the podGroup are successfully scheduled.

enrichment.problem: Scheduler profiles each maintained their own `waitingPods` list, so plugins could only see pods waiting in the permit stage for the current profile. This prevented cross‑profile visibility needed for use‑cases like coscheduling where all pods in a group must be considered together.
enrichment.affected: Scheduler users and plugin developers that rely on the permit‑stage waiting list, especially those using multiple scheduling profiles or implementing cross‑profile coordination such as coscheduling.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a shared `frameworkImpl.waitingPods` list that is common to the whole scheduler instance and added the `IterateOverWaitingPods` method. Any profile can now iterate over all pods in the scheduler that are in the permit stage, regardless of which profile they belong to.
enrichment.impact: Plugins that need to coordinate scheduling across multiple profiles (e.g., coscheduling, all‑or‑nothing workloads) can now obtain a complete view of waiting pods, simplifying implementation and improving correctness of multi‑profile scheduling scenarios.

feature.userFacingChange:
* Embed Node information into Pod-bound service account tokens as additional metadata
* Set the 'JTI' field in issued service account tokens, and embed this information as `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` in user's ExtraInfo

enrichment.problem: Pod-bound service account tokens did not include node-related metadata or a unique token identifier, making it difficult to correlate token usage with the node that created it for auditing or security purposes.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses pod-bound service account tokens—especially clusters that require node‑level audit logs or need to uniquely identify tokens for revocation.
enrichment.fix: The token issuance process now embeds node information and the JWT ID (JTI) into each service account token. This data is added to the token's ExtraInfo under the key `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id`.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and security by allowing clusters to trace token usage back to the originating node and uniquely identify each token instance, facilitating better audit trails and token revocation strategies.

feature.description: Introduced a new alpha feature gate, `SELinuxMount`, which can now be enabled to accelerate SELinux relabeling.
feature.author: jsafrane
feature.userFacingChange: New alpha feature gate `SELinuxMount` can be used to speed up SELinux relabeling of volumes.

enrichment.problem: SELinux relabeling of volumes on nodes can be slow, causing increased pod startup times in clusters with SELinux enabled.
enrichment.affected: Pods that mount volumes on nodes with SELinux enabled; kubelet processes handling volume mounts.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new alpha feature gate `SELinuxMount` that, when enabled, speeds up SELinux relabeling during volume mount operations.
enrichment.impact: Reduces pod startup latency and improves overall node performance for workloads that use SELinux, especially in storage‑intensive environments.

feature.description: Added a new metric `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` to measure the total number of API server encryption configuration reload successes and failures.  This metric now contains the `status` label with a value that is either `success` or `failure`. Deprecated the metrics `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_success_total` and `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_failure_total`. Please use `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` instead.
feature.author: aramase
feature.userFacingChange:
Added a new metric `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` to measure total number of
API server encryption configuration reload successes and failures.
This metric contains the `status` label with a value that is either `success` or `failure`.

Deprecated the metrics `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_success_total`
and `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_failure_total`.
Use `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` instead.

issueContext.title: Change encryption config reload success/failure metrics
issueContext.body:
Change encryption config controller reload metrics to be consistent with other places (Authn, Authz)
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4456/files#r1480546416

Combine `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_failures_total` and `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_success_total` into a single metric `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` with `status` with an enum value of `success` and `failure`.

/sig auth
/triage accepted

enrichment.problem: The API server exposed two separate metrics for encryption configuration reload successes and failures, which was inconsistent with other components and forced users to track two metrics for a single logical operation.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that scrape Prometheus metrics for API server encryption configuration reloads (e.g., monitoring dashboards, alerting rules).
enrichment.fix: Introduced a single metric `apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reloads_total` that includes a `status` label (values `success` or `failure`). Deprecated the old `*_success_total` and `*_failure_total` metrics.
enrichment.impact: Operators can simplify monitoring and alerting for encryption config reloads, using one metric with a label instead of two separate counters. Existing dashboards and alerts that reference the deprecated metrics need to be updated.

feature.description: "Added the `apiserver_watch_cache_read_wait` metric to measure the watch cache impact on request latency."
feature.author: padlar
feature.userFacingChange: Added apiserver_watch_cache_read_wait metric to measure watch cache impact on request latency.

issueContext.title: Implement `apiserver_watch_cache_read_wait` metric
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2340

From https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/2340-Consistent-reads-from-cache/README.md#what-if-the-watch-cache-is-stale 


> Metric apiserver_watch_cache_read_wait will measure wait time experienced by reads for watch cache to become fresh. If user notices a latency request in they can use this metric to confirm that the issue is caused by watch cache.

For now posted as a "help wanted" issue, however if we cannot hit the timeline for 1.30 code freeze ([5th March](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/tree/master/releases/release-1.30#summary)) I would take it over so we don't miss. Still issue is simple enough that it can be quickly implemented.

Implementation tips:
* Add a metric around waitUnitlFreshAndBlock method https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f07b47c3d1e596f53640285afb0d53a81fe6f259/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L441
* Metric should be a histogram with latency buckets similar to api latency
* Metric should have label for resource version.

### Why is this needed?

A way to monitor watch cache impact on request latency.

enrichment.problem: Operators had no dedicated metric to determine whether request latency was caused by the watch cache being stale, making it hard to diagnose performance issues related to watch cache reads.
enrichment.affected: Users of the Kubernetes API server who experience request latency, especially when the watch cache is stale.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `apiserver_watch_cache_read_wait` histogram metric in the kube-apiserver. It records the wait time for reads until the watch cache becomes fresh and includes a resourceVersion label for detailed analysis.
enrichment.impact: Provides clear visibility into watch‑cache‑induced latency, enabling faster identification and remediation of performance problems in the API server, improving overall cluster observability.

feature.description: The NodeLogQuery feature has been promoted to beta. No functional changes have been made from the alpha version.
feature.author: aravindhp
feature.userFacingChange: Promote the NodeLogQuery feature to beta. There have been no functional changes from alpha.

enrichment.problem: The NodeLogQuery feature was only available as an alpha feature, limiting its stability guarantees and preventing it from being used as a supported beta feature.
enrichment.affected: Users who want to query node logs on Linux or Windows nodes; clusters that enable the feature gate for NodeLogQuery.
enrichment.fix: Promoted NodeLogQuery from alpha to beta without changing its functionality, making the feature generally available under a beta feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now enable the NodeLogQuery beta feature on Linux and Windows nodes, allowing more reliable log querying for troubleshooting and observability while benefitting from tighter compatibility testing.

feature.description: Graduated "Forensic Container Checkpointing" (KEP #2008) from Alpha to Beta.
feature.author: adrianreber
feature.userFacingChange: Graduated _forensic container checkpointing_ [KEP #2008](https://kep.k8s.io/2008) from Alpha to Beta.

enrichment.problem: Forensic container checkpointing was only available as an alpha feature, which meant limited stability guarantees, optional enablement, and potential incompatibilities for users needing reliable state capture for debugging.
enrichment.affected: Users who perform container checkpointing for forensic or debugging purposes, and any node that runs a CRI runtime supporting the checkpointing APIs.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted from Alpha to Beta (KEP #2008). This graduation adds stronger API stability guarantees, enables the feature by default on clusters that meet the requirements, updates documentation, and incorporates additional validation and testing to make it production‑ready.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and developers can now rely on forensic container checkpointing in more environments, using it for debugging, post‑mortem analysis, and state capture with beta‑level confidence. It broadens the toolset for troubleshooting workloads without needing custom patches or experimental flags.

feature.description: The kubelet now rejects creating the pod if `hostUserns=false` and the CRI runtime does not support user namespaces.
feature.author: giuseppe
feature.userFacingChange: The Kubelet rejects creating the pod if hostUserns=false and the CRI runtime does not support user namespaces.

enrichment.problem: When a pod was configured with hostUserns=false, the kubelet did not verify whether the CRI runtime supported user namespaces. The pod could be accepted and later fail to start, leading to confusing errors for users.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request a non‑host user namespace on nodes where the CRI runtime does not implement user‑namespace support.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now validates the CRI runtime's support for user namespaces. If hostUserns is set to false and the runtime lacks support, pod creation is rejected immediately with an explicit error.
enrichment.impact: Users get immediate feedback instead of silent pod‑creation failures, preventing wasted resources and debugging time for workloads that rely on user namespaces.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go `1.22`.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go version, which could lead to build failures, missing language features, and lack of upstream security and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, as well as downstream distributors who recompile the binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to use Go 1.22 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are now built with the latest Go toolchain, bringing compiler optimizations, security patches, and new language features, while ensuring future releases remain compatible with Go's release cycle.

feature.description: Enhanced cloud provider integrations to support optional, per-Node custom labels that can be supplied and applied to Nodes by the node controller. These extra labels will only be applied where the cloud provider integration supports this feature.
feature.author: mmerkes
feature.userFacingChange:
Added support for cloud provider integrations to supply optional, per-Node custom labels that will be
applied to Nodes by the node controller.
Extra labels will only be applied where the cloud provider integration implements this.

enrichment.problem: Cloud provider integrations could not attach custom, provider‑specific labels to individual Nodes, limiting the ability to convey metadata needed for scheduling or tooling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using cloud provider integrations that implement the new optional label interface; the Node objects created/managed by those providers.
enrichment.fix: The node controller now accepts an optional set of per‑Node custom labels supplied by the cloud provider integration and applies them to the corresponding Node object, but only when the provider implements the new feature.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now expose provider‑specific information (e.g., region, instance type, special capabilities) as Node labels, enabling more precise node selection, policies, and observability without manual admin labeling.

feature.description: kube-apiserver now reports latency metric for JWT authenticator authenticate token decisions in the `apiserver_authentication_jwt_authenticator_latency_seconds` metric, labeled by jwtIssuer hash and result.
feature.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver did not expose any latency metrics for JWT token authentication, making it difficult for operators to monitor and troubleshoot authentication performance.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using JWT authentication for API access; administrators who rely on metrics for monitoring and alerting.
enrichment.fix: Adds the `apiserver_authentication_jwt_authenticator_latency_seconds` metric, which records the latency of JWT authenticator decisions. The metric is labeled with a hash of the JWT issuer and the authentication result (e.g., success or failure).
enrichment.impact: Provides observability into JWT authentication latency, enabling operators to detect slow token validation, set alerts, and improve security incident response. Improves overall cluster monitoring and debugging of auth flows.

feature.description: "`kubectl get job` now displays the status for the listed jobs."
feature.author: ivanvc

issueContext.title: Jobs should display whether or not they are suspended.
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Suspend is a GA feature and it is big component of Kueue.

It would be nice to display if jobs are suspended when doing `kubectl get job`.

```
kehannon@kehannon-thinkpadp1gen4i:~/Work/jobset/examples/startup-policy$ kubectl get jobs
NAME                                        COMPLETIONS   DURATION   AGE
pytorch-job                                 0/4           8d         8d
pytorch-workers-0                           1/4           8d         8d
success-policy-workers-0                    2/2           14s        8d
suspend-startup-driver-anyorder-driver-0    0/1                      10s
suspend-startup-driver-anyorder-workers-0   0/4                      10s
suspend-startup-driver-ready-driver-0       0/1                      49s
suspend-startup-driver-ready-workers-0      0/4                      49s
```
A new column that displays if the job is suspended would be helpful.

### Why is this needed?

Improve UX around suspend. Its a bit difficult to know why the job has not created pods unless you know about the suspend field.

enrichment.problem: kubectl get job output did not show whether a Job was suspended, making it hard to understand why a Job had no pods.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using `kubectl get job` to inspect Jobs, especially those leveraging the suspend feature in batch workloads.
enrichment.fix: Added a new column to the `kubectl get job` table that displays the Job's status, including the suspended flag.
enrichment.impact: Users can quickly see the suspension state of Jobs directly from the CLI, improving usability and reducing guesswork when troubleshooting batch workloads.

feature.description:
RemoteCommand feature gates for kubectl exec, cp, and attach over WebSockets are now enabled by default (Beta):
- Server-side feature gate: `TranslateStreamCloseWebsocketRequests`
- Client-side (kubectl) feature gate: `KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS`
- To disable RemoteCommand over WebSockets for kubectl, the environment variable feature gate must be explicitly set to `false`: `KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=false`.
feature.author: seans3
feature.userFacingChange:
- Feature gates for RemoteCommand (kubectl exec, cp, and attach) over WebSockets are now enabled by default (Beta).
  - Server-side feature gate: TranslateStreamCloseWebsocketRequests
  - Client-side (kubectl) feature gate: KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS
  - To turn off RemoteCommand over WebSockets for kubectl, the environment variable feature gate must be explicitly set - KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=false

enrichment.problem: RemoteCommand (kubectl exec, cp, attach) over WebSockets required manual feature gate activation, limiting its use and causing extra configuration for users who wanted the newer implementation.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users invoking exec, cp, or attach; clusters where the API server runs with the TranslateStreamCloseWebsocketRequests gate.
enrichment.fix: The RemoteCommand feature gates are now enabled by default (Beta). The server-side gate TranslateStreamCloseWebsocketRequests and the client-side gate KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS are on by default. Users can opt‑out by setting the environment variable KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS=false.
enrichment.impact: Users can run kubectl exec, cp, and attach over WebSockets without extra configuration, gaining the benefits of the newer RemoteCommand implementation (e.g., better stream handling). Existing workflows remain unchanged unless they intentionally disable the feature.

feature.description: kube-apiserver now reports metrics for authorization decisions in the `apiserver_authorization_decisions_total` metric, labeled by authorizer type, name, and decision.
feature.author: liggitt

issueContext.title: Add metrics for general authz decisions

enrichment.problem: The API server did not expose any metrics for authorization decisions, making it difficult for operators to observe, alert on, or debug authz behavior.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and monitoring systems that need visibility into authorization decisions; any workloads relying on authz debugging.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `apiserver_authorization_decisions_total` counter metric that records each authz decision, labeled by authorizer type, authorizer name, and the decision outcome (allow/deny).
enrichment.impact: Enables real‑time monitoring and alerting of authz activity, helps identify misconfigurations or unusual denial patterns, and improves overall cluster observability and security posture.

feature.description: "kubeadm: added the `WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents` feature gate. It could be used to tell kubeadm to wait for all control plane components to be ready when running "kubeadm init" or "kubeadm join --control-plane". Previously, kubeadm only waited for the kube-apiserver. The "kubeadm join" workflow now includes a new experimental phase called "wait-control-plane". This phase was marked as non-experimental when WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents became GA. Accordingly, a "kubeadm init" phase "wait-control-plane" was also available once WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents became GA. These phases could be skipped if the user preferred not to wait for the control plane components."
feature.author: neolit123
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: add the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate. It can be used to tell kubeadm to wait for all control plane components to be ready when running "kubeadm init" or "kubeadm join --control-plane". Currently kubeadm only waits for the kube-apiserver. The "kubeadm join" workflow now includes a new experimental phase called "wait-control-plane". This phase will be marked as non-experimental when WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents becomes GA. Accordingly a "kubeadm init" phase "wait-control-plane" will also be available once WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents becomes GA. These phases can be skipped if the user prefers to not wait for the control plane components.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm only waited for the kube-apiserver to become ready during "kubeadm init" and "kubeadm join --control-plane", so the bootstrap could finish while other control‑plane components (controller‑manager, scheduler, etc.) were still starting, leading to race conditions and failures for workloads that expect the full control plane to be up.
enrichment.affected: Users running "kubeadm init" or "kubeadm join --control-plane" to create or add control‑plane nodes. Also affects any automation or scripts that assume the control plane is fully up after kubeadm returns.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents feature gate and a new "wait-control-plane" phase (initially experimental) for both "kubeadm init" and "kubeadm join --control-plane". When enabled, kubeadm waits for all control‑plane components to report ready before completing. The phase can be skipped if the user prefers.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of cluster bootstrapping by ensuring the entire control plane is ready before proceeding, reducing post‑bootstrap errors and making automated provisioning more predictable.

feature.description: "Updated `ImageGCMaxAge` behavior in the kubelet to wait the `MaxAge` duration after the kubelet has restarted before garbage collecting."
feature.author: haircommander
feature.userFacingChange: Update ImageGCMaxAge behavior in the kubelet to wait the MaxAge duration after the kubelet has restarted before garbage collecting

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet restarts, the ImageGCMaxAge timer was not respected, causing immediate image garbage collection. This could delete recently used images before the MaxAge period elapsed, leading to unnecessary image pulls and delayed pod startups.
enrichment.affected: All workloads running on nodes where the kubelet restarts and relies on ImageGCMaxAge for image retention. Particularly affects clusters with frequent node restarts or short MaxAge settings.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now defers image garbage collection until the full MaxAge duration has passed after a restart. The ImageGCMaxAge timer is reset on restart and only triggers GC after that period.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that restart (e.g., during upgrades or failures) will retain images for the configured MaxAge, avoiding extra image pulls and reducing pod startup latency. This improves node stability and reduces network and registry load.

feature.description: Added a "reason" field to the "image_garbage_collected_total" metric, allowing administrators to differentiate between images that were collected for reasons "age" vs "space".
feature.author: haircommander
feature.userFacingChange: Add "reason" field to image_garbage_collected_total metric, so admins can differentiate images that were collected for reason "age" vs "space"

enrichment.problem: Cluster administrators could not tell why images were removed by garbage collection, as the image_garbage_collected_total metric lacked a dimension to indicate the cause (age‑based vs space‑based collection).
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and monitoring systems that rely on image garbage‑collection metrics to observe node health and storage usage.
enrichment.fix: The metric image_garbage_collected_total now includes a new "reason" label with possible values "age" and "space", allowing the cause of each collection event to be distinguished.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability of node image garbage collection, enabling admins to better understand and troubleshoot image churn, plan capacity, and tune image retention policies.

feature.description: Revised node selection based on container image location. The kube-scheduler now considers whether nodes have the required images available for init containers, and for sidecar containers if the cluster has 'SidecarContainers' enabled.
feature.author: kerthcet
feature.userFacingChange:
Revised node selection based on container image location.
The kube-scheduler now considers whether nodes have the images available for init containers, and
for sidecar containers if the cluster has `SidecarContainers` enabled.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler previously ignored whether a node already had the container images needed for init containers (and sidecar containers when the SidecarContainers feature is enabled), which could lead to pods being placed on nodes that would have to pull those images, causing longer start‑up times and unnecessary network traffic.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use init containers or sidecar containers (when SidecarContainers feature is enabled) could be scheduled to nodes lacking the needed images, leading to delays.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑scheduler now evaluates image locality during node selection: it prefers nodes that already have the required images for init containers, and for sidecar containers if the cluster has the SidecarContainers feature gate enabled.
enrichment.impact: Pods with init containers or sidecars start faster and with less network overhead, improving overall pod launch performance and reducing load on container registries.

feature.description: "kubeadm: Added support for machine-readable output with `-o yaml` and `-o json` to the command `kubeadm certs check-expiration`. This change is introduced in a new API: ``` kind: CertificateExpirationInfo apiVersion: output.kubeadm.k8s.io/v1alpha3 ``` The existing non-structured formatting is preserved. The output API version v1alpha2 is now deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please migrate to using v1alpha3."
feature.author: carlory
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: add support for machine readable output with "-o yaml" and "-o json" to the command "kubeadm certs check-expiration". This change is added in a new API "kind": "CertificateExpirationInfo",  "apiVersion": "output.kubeadm.k8s.io/v1alpha3". The existing non structured formatting is preserved. The output API version v1alpha2 is now deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please migrate to using v1alpha3.

enrichment.problem: The `kubeadm certs check-expiration` command only produced human‑readable text, making it difficult to parse programmatically. Additionally, the existing structured output API version v1alpha2 is deprecated and will be removed.
enrichment.affected: Administrators and automation scripts that run `kubeadm certs check-expiration` to monitor certificate lifetimes, especially those that previously used the v1alpha2 output format.
enrichment.fix: Added `-o yaml` and `-o json` flags to `kubeadm certs check-expiration`, exposing a new API version `output.kubeadm.k8s.io/v1alpha3` with kind `CertificateExpirationInfo`. The original human‑readable format is preserved. Users are instructed to migrate from v1alpha2 to v1alpha3.
enrichment.impact: Scripts and automation tools can now reliably consume certificate expiration data, improving cluster maintenance workflows. Users relying on the old v1alpha2 format must update their tooling before the version is removed.

feature.description: "kubectl `port-forward` over websockets (tunneling SPDY) can now be enabled using an `Alpha` feature flag environment variable: KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS=true. The API Server being communicated to must *also* have an `Alpha` feature flag enabled: PortForwardWebsockets."
feature.author: seans3
feature.userFacingChange: - kubectl port-forward over websockets (tunneling SPDY) can be enabled using an `Alpha` feature flag environment variable: KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS=true. The API Server being communicated to must *also* have an `Alpha` feature flag enabled: PortForwardWebsockets.

enrichment.problem: kubectl port-forward only supported SPDY and could not use websockets, limiting testing and future enhancements.
enrichment.affected: Kubectl users invoking port-forward who need websocket support, and API servers that must enable the corresponding Alpha flag.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an Alpha feature flag (environment variable KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS=true) that enables port-forward over websockets. The target API server must also enable the matching Alpha flag (PortForwardWebsockets).
enrichment.impact: Allows users and developers to test and use websocket-based port-forwarding, providing a path toward more flexible and potentially more performant port-forward implementations.

feature.description: LoadBalancerIPMode feature is now marked as Beta.
feature.author: rikatz

enrichment.problem: The LoadBalancerIPMode feature was only available as an alpha feature, requiring a feature gate and lacking default enablement, limiting its use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Users creating Service objects of type LoadBalancer that need to control the IP mode (e.g., IPv4 vs IPv6 or dual‑stack).
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to Beta (KEP-1860), making the feature gate enabled by default and stabilizing the Service spec field for IP mode selection.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use the LoadBalancerIPMode field for Services without extra feature‑gate configuration, enabling more reliable dual‑stack or specific IP mode setups in production workloads.

feature.description: Promoted the `ImageMaximumGCAge` feature to beta.
feature.author: haircommander
feature.userFacingChange: Promote ImageMaximumGCAge feature to beta

enrichment.problem: The ImageMaximumGCAge feature was only available as an alpha feature gate, requiring manual enablement and lacking the stability guarantees of a higher maturity level.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet image garbage collection on nodes; administrators who manage node disk space and image lifecycle.
enrichment.fix: Promoted ImageMaximumGCAge to beta, making it enabled by default (or easier to enable) and providing a more stable, supported implementation for configuring the maximum age of images retained by the garbage collector.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now reliably control how long unused container images are kept on nodes, helping to manage node disk usage and prevent unexpected image buildup without relying on an alpha feature.

feature.description: Added feature gate `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` for enabling mutation policy in admission chain.
feature.author: cici37
feature.userFacingChange: Add feature gate `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` for enabling mutation policy in admission chain.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes had no way to enable the new MutatingAdmissionPolicy feature, preventing clusters from using policy-driven mutation in the admission chain.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that want to use MutatingAdmissionPolicy; control‑plane components that process admission (primarily the API server).
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new feature gate `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` that can be turned on to activate mutation policies during admission processing.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can now opt‑in to MutatingAdmissionPolicy, allowing fine‑grained, declarative mutation of objects via admission policies, improving flexibility and future feature evolution.

feature.description: Graduated HorizontalPodAutoscaler support for per-container metrics to stable.
feature.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) only supported aggregate pod metrics in earlier releases; per‑container metrics were only available in alpha/beta, preventing stable production use of fine‑grained autoscaling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using HPA that need fine‑grained scaling per container; operators and developers who previously avoided per‑container metrics due to stability concerns.
enrichment.fix: The per‑container metrics feature for HPA has been graduated to GA (stable), making the API and controller behavior stable and fully supported.
enrichment.impact: Users can now reliably configure HPA to scale based on individual container resource usage in production workloads, with full version‑skew guarantees and without relying on experimental APIs.

feature.description: Added `client-go` support for upgrading subresource fields from client-side to server-side management.
feature.author: erikgb

enrichment.problem: client-go required callers to manually handle upgrades of subresource fields, leading to extra boilerplate and risk of inconsistencies when the server changed its upgrade handling.
enrichment.affected: Developers building controllers or operators that interact with resources via client-go and rely on subresource field upgrades.
enrichment.fix: client-go now delegates the upgrade of subresource fields to the server, automatically handling the transition from client-side to server-side management.
enrichment.impact: Developers using client-go no longer need custom code for subresource field upgrades, reducing complexity and preventing potential bugs. The change aligns client behavior with server semantics and improves compatibility with future server upgrades.

feature.description: "In the Pod API, setting the alpha `procMount` field to `Unmasked` in a container now required setting `spec.hostUsers=false` as well."
feature.author: haircommander
feature.userFacingChange: In the Pod API, setting the alpha `procMount` field to `Unmasked` in a container now requires setting `spec.hostUsers=false` as well.

enrichment.problem: When configuring a container with the alpha procMount field set to Unmasked, the API previously allowed it without any other settings. This caused validation inconsistencies because Unmasked procMount requires hostUsers to be disabled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the alpha procMount=Unmasked field without also disabling hostUsers. Typically workloads that need unmasked /proc access.
enrichment.fix: The Pod API now validates that spec.hostUsers is set to false whenever procMount is set to Unmasked. Manifests that omit this will be rejected until the required field is added.

issueContext.title: CEL in Admission(ValidatingAdmissionPolicy): explicitly excluding resources from validatingadmissionpolicy interception
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?
Currently, the vap only prevent itself and the binding from being intercepted: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/admission.go#L189-L197
We would love to revisit this before going to GA to make sure if we wanna explicitly prevent any other resources as well.

Thanks for the suggestion from @liggitt : "propose excluding tokenreviews / subjectaccessreviews from validatingadmissionpolicy interception"

### Why is this needed?

It's too easy to brick delegated authn / authz in a cluster if user-configurable policy can break subjectaccessreview / tokenreview specifically.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could intercept TokenReview, SelfSubjectReview, LocalSubjectAccessReview, and SubjectAccessReview resources, allowing user-defined policies to unintentionally block core authentication and authorization calls, potentially bricking delegated authn/authz.

enrichment.fix: The admission plugin now explicitly excludes those four resources from validation for all versions of the authentication.k8s.io and authorization.k8s.io API groups, ensuring they bypass VAP interception.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can no longer be rendered inoperable by misconfigured ValidatingAdmissionPolicy rules that affect token or access review operations, preserving reliable authentication/authorization flows and improving overall security and stability.

other.author: linxiulei
