issueContext.title: Serving watch requests takes large memory space in goroutine's stack
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Optimize the memory usage of goroutine stack for serving watch requests. According to the [traceback](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117777#issuecomment-1723055664) of handling a watch request, the stack memory is 0x3768, which is very close to 16 KiB and Golang runtime will double it to 32 KiB once exceeded. In fact, it does exceed if we print the traceback deeper and take the fact that extra stack memory reserved by Golang itself into consideration. 

A naive optimization is to run as much as preparation handlers in a separate goroutine and then move the actual serving to another goroutine, so the former routine can free the stack memory earlier and make it more memory efficient.

### Why is this needed?

Given the extensive use of watch requests, 32 KiB per watch could add up to a very high amount of memory overhead for `kube-apiserver`. A typical watch request commonly lasts for 30s or longer, which means this memory will be active for quite long. I see a great improvement in memory efficiency to do this optimization.

enrichment.problem: Serving watch requests in kube-apiserver consumes up to ~32 KiB of stack memory per goroutine, leading to high overall memory usage for long‑running watches.
enrichment.affected: kube-apiserver handling watch requests; clusters with many watch clients are affected.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an optimization that runs preparation handlers in a separate goroutine and serves the watch in another, allowing the first goroutine's stack to be freed earlier. The optimization is enabled by default and can be disabled with the feature gate APIServingWithRoutine=false.
enrichment.impact: Reduces per‑watch memory overhead, decreasing total apiserver memory consumption especially in clusters with many or long‑lived watch connections, improving scalability and stability.

issueContext.title: sched framework: expose NodeInfo in all functions of PluginsRunner interface
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Scheduler framework exposes a series of functions in PluginsRunner interface for out-of-tree plugins to implement custom functionalities:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6f8d38406a7f16fc9cc9b72789a9b826105b1b54/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L601-L605

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6f8d38406a7f16fc9cc9b72789a9b826105b1b54/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L725-L750

However, `RunPreScorePlugins` and `RunScorePlugins` exposes `Node` instead of `NodeInfo` like other functions. It causes inconvenient UX for plugin users like [koordinator](https://github.com/koordinator-sh/koordinator). For example, one of the requirements is to find an optimal preemption candidate node in PostFilter plugins. `NodeInfo` carries important extra info during the preemption dryrun, and w/o consuming `NodeInfo`, running `Run{Pre}ScorePlugins` would be non-sense. To work around it, users have to plumb very specific and sometime ugly semantics themselves which should have been avoided.

### Why is this needed?

- consistent function signature - all use NodeInfo
- unleash more potential to use scheduler framework natively w/o hacks

enrichment.problem: Scheduler framework functions used inconsistent types: RunPreScorePlugins, RunScorePlugins, PreScore, Extender Filter and Prioritize accepted a Node object instead of NodeInfo, making it hard for out-of-tree plugins (e.g., Koordinator) to access needed node metadata and forcing hacky workarounds.
enrichment.affected: Any out‑of‑tree scheduler plugins or extenders that implement the updated interfaces – e.g., Koordinator, custom pre‑score, score, filter, or prioritize plugins.
enrichment.fix: Updated the signatures of PluginsRunner, PreScorePlugin, and Extender interfaces to accept NodeInfo instead of Node, providing a consistent API across all scheduler plugin calls.
enrichment.impact: Plugins and extenders can now reliably use full node metadata during pre-score, scoring, filtering, and prioritization without custom workarounds, enabling cleaner implementations and unlocking richer scheduling features such as accurate preemption decisions.

other.description: "Removed the generally available feature gate `MinimizeIPTablesRestore`."
other.author: ty-dc

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `MinimizeIPTablesRestore` was removed, so clusters can no longer enable or disable this behavior via a feature gate.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that had explicitly set `MinimizeIPTablesRestore` in kube‑proxy configuration. The change only affects the kube‑proxy component.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate definition was deleted, making the MinimizeIPTablesRestore behavior fixed (always on) and removing the associated command‑line/config flag.
enrichment.impact: Users no longer need to manage the feature gate; the iptables‑restore minimization is always applied. Existing configurations that referenced the gate must be cleaned up, but runtime behavior does not change.

other.description: Removed the GA feature gate for `IPTablesOwnershipCleanup` in version `1.30`.
other.author: bzsuni

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `IPTablesOwnershipCleanup` was still exposed, allowing users to enable or disable the cleanup of iptables ownerships, which is now always on.
enrichment.affected: Users who had the feature gate enabled or disabled in their kube-proxy configuration. Clusters running custom `--feature-gates=IPTablesOwnershipCleanup=...` will see the flag ignored after upgrade.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is removed in v1.30, making IPTables ownership cleanup permanently enabled and no longer configurable via a flag.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to manage the `IPTablesOwnershipCleanup` flag. The behavior is consistent across all installations, reducing configuration complexity and preventing accidental disabling of the cleanup logic.

other.description: "Removed the generally available feature gate `KubeletPodResourcesGetAllocatable`."
other.author: ii2day
other.userFacingChange: Removed generally available feature gate `KubeletPodResourcesGetAllocatable`.

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `KubeletPodResourcesGetAllocatable` was removed, so any kubelet configuration that still references this gate will be rejected or ignored.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where administrators have manually enabled the `KubeletPodResourcesGetAllocatable` feature gate in the kubelet config.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been eliminated from the codebase. Users should delete `KubeletPodResourcesGetAllocatable` from their kubelet configuration files; the underlying behavior is now always enabled by default.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kubelet start‑up failures due to unknown feature gates and simplifies configuration. No functional change for workloads, but administrators must update configs to avoid errors.

other.description: "Removed the generally available feature gate `KubeletPodResources`."
other.author: bzsuni
other.userFacingChange: Removed generally available feature gate `KubeletPodResources`.

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `KubeletPodResources` was still available for users to set, but it is now removed. Clusters that reference this gate in their kubelet configuration will encounter validation errors.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that manually set the `KubeletPodResources` feature gate in kubelet configuration files or command‑line flags.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been removed from the kubelet binary and its documentation. The functionality it guarded is now permanently enabled (or permanently disabled) and no longer configurable via a gate.
enrichment.impact: Administrators must delete any `KubeletPodResources` entries from the kubelet config or command line. After the change the kubelet will operate with the default behavior, eliminating the need to manage the gate and reducing configuration complexity.

other.description: When working with client-go events, it's now recommended to use `NewEventBroadcasterAdapterWithContext` instead of `NewEventBroadcasterAdapter` if contextual logging support is needed.
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: client-go events: `NewEventBroadcasterAdapterWithContext` should be used instead of `NewEventBroadcasterAdapter` if the goal is to support contextual logging.

enrichment.problem: Using NewEventBroadcasterAdapter does not include contextual logging, so event-related logs lack request/operation context, making troubleshooting harder.
enrichment.affected: Applications or controllers that use client-go's event broadcasting and need context-aware logs.
enrichment.fix: Introduce NewEventBroadcasterAdapterWithContext and recommend its use for event broadcasting when contextual logging is desired. The new adapter propagates the provided context to log entries.
enrichment.impact: Provides richer, context-aware logs for components that emit events via client-go, improving observability and debugging without changing runtime behavior.

other.description: Updated cni-plugins to version `v1.4.0`.
other.author: saschagrunert
other.userFacingChange: Updated cni-plugins to v1.4.0.

enrichment.problem: Clusters were using older CNI plugin version (v1.3.x) that lacked recent bug fixes, performance improvements, and security patches, which could lead to networking glitches or missing features.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that rely on the built‑in CNI plugins (installed via kubelet) on Linux node pools.
enrichment.fix: The node component (kubelet) now ships with CNI plugins updated to v1.4.0, bringing in upstream bug fixes, enhancements, and security updates.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability and security of pod networking for all clusters using the default CNI plugins on Linux nodes, reducing potential network‑related failures.

other.description: Migrated the kube-proxy to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging).
other.author: fatsheep9146
other.userFacingChange: Migrated the cmd/kube-proxy to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging).

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy logs were not contextual, making it harder for operators to correlate log entries with specific network rules or pods during troubleshooting.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and any workloads that rely on kube-proxy for service traffic; debugging and monitoring tools that ingest kube-proxy logs.
enrichment.fix: Migrated cmd/kube-proxy to use the new contextual logging framework, adding request IDs and relevant fields to each log entry.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now more easily filter and trace proxy behavior, speeding up debugging of network traffic issues and improving overall observability of the networking stack.

other.description: "Migrated `client-go/metadata` to contextual logging."
other.author: ricardoapl
other.userFacingChange: Migrate client-go/metadata to contextual logging

enrichment.problem: client-go/metadata package emitted logs without attaching request context, making it difficult to correlate log lines with specific API calls or operations.
enrichment.affected: Any component that imports client-go/metadata (e.g., kube-apiserver, controller-manager, custom controllers, and other clients) now gets contextual log messages.
enrichment.fix: Migrated the metadata client to use contextual logging as defined in KEP 3077, now obtaining a logger from the request context (klog.LoggerFrom) and passing it through all metadata client calls.
enrichment.impact: Improves debuggability and observability for components that use the metadata client by providing request-scoped log entries, leading to clearer diagnostics and consistent logging across the codebase.

other.description: "Updated cri-tools to `v1.29.0`."
other.author: saschagrunert
other.userFacingChange: Updated cri-tools to v1.29.0.

enrichment.problem: The cluster used an older version of cri-tools, which could miss upstream bug fixes, new CRI features, and compatibility improvements for container runtimes.
enrichment.affected: Any workflows, tests, or components that rely on cri-tools (e.g., kubelet integration tests, CI pipelines, and developers using the CRI command‑line utilities).
enrichment.fix: The cri-tools dependency was upgraded to version v1.29.0, bringing the latest upstream changes into the Kubernetes codebase.
enrichment.impact: Users benefit from up‑to‑date CRI validation tools, improved compatibility with newer container runtimes, and any bug fixes or feature enhancements introduced in cri-tools v1.29.0.

other.description: "resource.k8s.io/ResourceClaim (alpha API): The strategic merge patch strategy for the `status.reservedFor` array was changed so that a strategic-merge-patch can now add individual entries. This change may break clients using strategic merge patch to update status, which rely on the previous behavior (replacing the entire array)."
other.author: pohly
other.userFacingChange: resource.k8s.io/ResourceClaim (alpha API): the strategic merge patch strategy for the `status.reservedFor` array was changed such that a strategic-merge-patch can add individual entries. This breaks clients using strategic merge patch to update status which rely on the previous behavior (replacing the entire array).

enrichment.problem: The strategic‑merge‑patch strategy for the `status.reservedFor` array in the alpha ResourceClaim API was changed. Clients that used a strategic‑merge‑patch to update the status expecting the entire array to be replaced now see only the new entries added, causing incorrect status updates.
enrichment.affected: Applications or controllers that patch `ResourceClaim.status.reservedFor` with a strategic‑merge‑patch and assume the array is fully replaced.
enrichment.fix: The patch handling was updated so that a strategic‑merge‑patch can add individual entries to `status.reservedFor` instead of always replacing the whole array.
enrichment.impact: Clients that rely on the previous replace‑entire‑array behavior must modify their patch logic (e.g., use a full replace patch or adjust to the merge behavior) to avoid stale or incomplete `reservedFor` entries.

other.description: `kube-proxy` nftables mode is now compatible with kernel `5.4`.
other.author: tnqn
other.userFacingChange: kube-proxy nftables mode is now compatible with kernel 5.4

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy running in nftables mode could not operate correctly on Linux kernels 5.4, causing packet filtering or service routing failures.
enrichment.affected: Users running kube-proxy in nftables mode on nodes with Linux kernel 5.4 experienced broken service traffic handling.
enrichment.fix: Implemented kernel‑5.4 compatibility adjustments in the nftables code path of kube-proxy, allowing the feature to work without errors on that kernel version.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use kube-proxy with nftables on kernel 5.4 can now start and route traffic reliably, eliminating service disruption for those environments.

other.description: Added warning for `PV` on reclaim policy when it is `Recycle`.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: add warning for PV on relaim policy when it is Recycle

enrichment.problem: PersistentVolumes created with the `Recycle` reclaim policy did not produce any indication that the policy is deprecated, leading users to unintentionally use a policy that is slated for removal.
enrichment.affected: Any workflow that creates or updates a PersistentVolume with `reclaimPolicy: Recycle`, including administrators and automation tools.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes now emits a warning when a PV is created or updated with the `Recycle` reclaim policy, alerting users to the deprecation and encouraging migration to supported policies (`Retain` or `Delete`).
enrichment.impact: Users receive early notice of a deprecated feature, reducing the risk of future operational surprises or failures when the policy is eventually removed. No functional change to existing PVs, only an informational warning.

other.description: "Fixed an issue where `kubectl apply` could panic when imported as a library."
other.author: Jefftree
other.userFacingChange: Fix an issue where kubectl apply could panic when imported as a library

enrichment.problem: `kubectl apply` could panic (crash) when its code was imported and used as a Go library, causing the host program to terminate unexpectedly.
enrichment.affected: Go programs that import the `kubectl apply` package as a library (custom CLI tools, CI jobs, automation scripts).
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks and error handling in the apply implementation to prevent the panic when the package is used as a library.
enrichment.impact: Programs that embed `kubectl apply` as a library no longer crash, improving stability for custom tooling, CI pipelines, and other automation that rely on the library.

other.description: The feature gate `LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking` (GA since 1.28) is now removed because the feature is unconditionally enabled.
other.author: Rei1010
other.userFacingChange: The feature gate `LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking` (GA since 1.28) is now removed, since the feature is unconditionally enabled.

enrichment.problem: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking feature gate remained in the codebase even though the feature has been GA and is now always enabled, leading to possible confusion or configuration errors for users who still set the flag.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have the LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking feature gate enabled in kube-apiserver or other component configs. Users upgrading from 1.28+ who still set the flag.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is removed from all components, making the feature unconditionally enabled and eliminating the need for users to specify the flag.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgrading to the new release no longer need to manage the LegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking flag. Existing configurations that set the flag will be ignored or cause validation errors, so users should clean up any references.

other.description: "Removed the GA feature gate `RemoveSelfLink`."
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: remove GA featuregate RemoveSelfLink

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `RemoveSelfLink` was left in the codebase even though the feature is fully rolled out, leaving an unnecessary configuration flag.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that had the `RemoveSelfLink` feature gate explicitly set in component flags (e.g., kube-apiserver) during upgrade.
enrichment.fix: The `RemoveSelfLink` feature gate has been removed from all component binaries, making the self‑link removal behavior permanent and eliminating the flag.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to set or manage this flag. Any existing `--feature-gates=RemoveSelfLink=...` settings will cause a startup error, so administrators must remove the flag during upgrade. No functional behavior changes for workloads.

other.description: "`kubeadm completion` error message now displayed supported shell types when an invalid shell was specified."
other.author: SataQiu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: show the supported shell types of 'kubeadm completion' in the error message when an invalid shell was specified

enrichment.problem: When users ran `kubeadm completion` with an unsupported shell type, the error message did not indicate which shell types are actually supported, causing confusion.
enrichment.affected: Administrators invoking `kubeadm completion` with an invalid shell argument.
enrichment.fix: The command now includes a list of supported shell types in the error output when an invalid shell argument is provided.
enrichment.impact: Improves the user experience for cluster administrators using kubeadm completion, making it easier to correct mistakes and accelerate setup.

other.description: Deprecated the `azureFile` in-tree storage plugin.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: removed the deprecated `azureFile` in-tree storage plugin

enrichment.problem: The in-tree `azureFile` storage plugin was deprecated and still present in the codebase, causing potential confusion and maintenance overhead for clusters that relied on it.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the in-tree `azureFile` storage plugin for PersistentVolume provisioning. Administrators will need to update their storage classes and PVC definitions to reference the Azure File CSI driver.
enrichment.fix: The deprecated `azureFile` in-tree storage plugin has been removed from the Kubernetes source. Users must now use the Azure File CSI driver for Azure File volumes.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that still use the in-tree `azureFile` driver will no longer be able to provision Azure File volumes; they must migrate to the CSI driver to continue using Azure File storage.

other.description: "Locked the GA feature-gate `ConsistentHTTPGetHandlers` to default."
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: Lock GA feature-gate ConsistentHTTPGetHandlers to default

enrichment.problem: The ConsistentHTTPGetHandlers feature gate was configurable even after reaching GA, allowing clusters to disable the default, consistent HTTP GET handling for probes, which could lead to inconsistent behavior.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet configurations that set ConsistentHTTPGetHandlers to false; all workloads that rely on HTTP GET readiness/liveness probes.
enrichment.fix: The GA feature gate ConsistentHTTPGetHandlers is now locked to its default value (enabled), removing the ability for users to change it via the kubelet configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that previously disabled this feature will now have consistent HTTP GET handling for health checks, eliminating potential inconsistencies and simplifying kubelet configuration.

other.description: Promoted feature-gate `LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp` to GA and locked it to default.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: Promote feature-gate LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp to GA and lock to default

enrichment.problem: The LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp feature was previously behind a feature gate, requiring clusters to manually enable it to remove legacy service account tokens, which could leave clusters with insecure long‑lived tokens.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that create service accounts, especially those that have been running with the feature gate disabled or in older versions.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp is promoted to GA and locked to its default (enabled) state, ensuring the cleanup of legacy service account tokens runs automatically in all clusters.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to opt‑in to token cleanup, reducing administrative overhead and improving cluster security by guaranteeing removal of deprecated service account tokens.

other.description: The in-tree cloud provider for Azure has now been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and CSI driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-azure instead.
other.author: nilo19

enrichment.problem: The built‑in (in‑tree) Azure cloud provider was removed from the Kubernetes code base, so clusters that still rely on it can no longer create or manage Azure resources through the kubelet, controller‑manager, or scheduler.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that were using the in‑tree Azure cloud provider for node provisioning, load balancer services, and storage integration.
enrichment.fix: Migrate to the external Azure cloud provider and the accompanying CSI driver located at https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud‑provider‑azure. Deploy the external cloud‑provider as a separate component and configure the cluster to use it.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using the removed in‑tree Azure provider must update their configuration before upgrading Kubernetes, otherwise cloud‑related functionality (e.g., load‑balancer provisioning, volume handling) will stop working.

other.description: The in-tree cloud provider for vSphere has been deprecated and removed. Users are advised to utilize the external cloud provider and CSI driver available at https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-vsphere.
other.author: dims
other.userFacingChange: The in-tree cloud provider for vSphere has now been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and CSI driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-vsphere instead.

enrichment.problem: The built‑in (in‑tree) vSphere cloud provider was deprecated and has now been removed from Kubernetes, causing clusters that rely on it for vSphere integration (node registration, load balancer services, volume provisioning, etc.) to lose those capabilities.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters running on vSphere that were configured to use the in‑tree cloud provider (cloud‑controller‑manager and related components).
enrichment.fix: The change removes the in‑tree implementation and directs users to adopt the external cloud‑provider and CSI driver published at https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-vsphere.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that still use the in‑tree vSphere cloud provider will fail to start or lose functionality unless they migrate to the external provider and CSI driver. Migration is required for continued vSphere support.

other.description: The `--cidr-allocator-type` option set to `CloudAllocator` for `kube-controller-manager` will be deprecated and removed in a future release. Users are advised to transition to and explore the available options provided by their external cloud provider.
other.author: dims

enrichment.problem: The `--cidr-allocator-type=CloudAllocator` flag for kube-controller-manager is deprecated and will be removed, causing clusters that still set this flag to fail to start or lose CIDR allocation functionality.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that configure kube-controller-manager with `--cidr-allocator-type=CloudAllocator`, typically in cloud environments.
enrichment.fix: The flag will be removed in a future release. Users must stop using `--cidr-allocator-type=CloudAllocator` and adopt the CIDR allocation mechanisms provided by their external cloud provider.
enrichment.impact: Ensures clusters remain functional after the removal by prompting administrators to update controller‑manager configuration. Prevents startup failures and aligns CIDR allocation with cloud‑provider implementations.

other.description: etcd image `v3.5.12` has been built.
other.author: bzsuni
other.userFacingChange: Build etcd image v3.5.12

enrichment.problem: Clusters were using older etcd images; a newer upstream etcd version was released but not yet built as an official Kubernetes image.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that run the etcd data store, especially those upgrading control‑plane components to use the new image.
enrichment.fix: Built and published the official etcd Docker image version v3.5.12, making it available for use by Kubernetes control-plane components.
enrichment.impact: Allows clusters to upgrade to the latest etcd release, which includes upstream bug fixes and security patches, improving reliability and security of the data store.

other.description:
Updated an audit annotation key used by the `…/serviceaccounts/<name>/token` resource handler.
The annotation used to persist the issued credential identifier is now `authentication.kubernetes.io/issued-credential-id`.
other.author: munnerz
other.userFacingChange:
Updated an audit annotation key used by the `…/serviceaccounts/<name>/token` resource handler.
The annotation used to persist the issued credential identifier is now `authentication.kubernetes.io/issued-credential-id`.

enrichment.problem: The audit logs for the serviceaccount token endpoint used an outdated annotation key to store the issued credential identifier, making it harder for auditors and tooling to reliably locate this information.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that rely on audit logs for service account token issuance; security teams and compliance tools that parse the credential ID annotation.
enrichment.fix: The resource handler for `…/serviceaccounts/<name>/token` now writes the identifier to the annotation `authentication.kubernetes.io/issued-credential-id` instead of the previous key.
enrichment.impact: Auditing and security tooling can now consistently retrieve the issued credential ID from audit events, improving traceability and compliance. Existing tooling that expects the old key may need to be updated.

other.description: Fixed a bug in scheduler requeueing where registered wildcard cluster event sources didn't work.
other.author: kerthcet
other.userFacingChange: Fixed a bug where registered wildcard clusterEvent sources didn't work in scheduler requeueing.

enrichment.problem: Wildcard clusterEvent sources registered with the scheduler were ignored during requeueing, causing the scheduler to miss relevant cluster-wide events.
enrichment.affected: Users configuring the scheduler with wildcard clusterEvent sources (e.g., custom scheduler plugins or frameworks) experienced missed events during requeue, potentially leading to stale scheduling decisions.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was updated to correctly handle registered wildcard clusterEvent sources during requeue operations, ensuring those events trigger the intended scheduling logic.
enrichment.impact: Schedulers that rely on wildcard clusterEvent sources now receive proper notifications, leading to correct pod placement and preventing missed scheduling opportunities.

other.description: "Updated `etcd` to version `3.5.12`."
other.author: bzsuni
other.userFacingChange: Update etcd to version 3.5.12

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes control plane components rely on an embedded etcd datastore; keeping etcd up to date is necessary to incorporate upstream bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the built‑in etcd (the default control‑plane setup) when installing or upgrading Kubernetes.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm/kubernetes release upgrades the bundled etcd binary from the previous version to 3.5.12, so new clusters and upgraded clusters will run etcd 3.5.12.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that create a new control‑plane or perform a version upgrade will benefit from the latest etcd stability, security, and performance improvements without manual intervention.

other.description: "Updated `distroless-iptables` to `v0.5.0`, debian-base to `bookworm-v1.0.1`, and setcap to `bookworm-v1.0.1`."
other.author: cpanato
