enrichment.problem: Older distroless-iptables, debian-base, and setcap images used by Kubernetes components were outdated, potentially missing security patches and bug fixes.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes components that bundle or use the distroless-iptables, debian-base, and setcap images, primarily kube-proxy and related test images.
enrichment.fix: Updated distroless-iptables to v0.5.0 and upgraded debian-base and setcap images to the bookworm-v1.0.1 release, incorporating the latest upstream updates.
enrichment.impact: Components that rely on these images (e.g., kube-proxy and related testing images) now run with newer OS libraries and security patches, reducing vulnerability exposure and improving stability.

other.description: "kubeadm: ensured that a variety of API server requests were retried during "init", "join", "upgrade", "reset" workflows. Prior to this change, some API server requests, such as creating or updating ConfigMaps, were "one-shot" - i.e., they could fail if the API server dropped connectivity for a very short period of time."
other.author: neolit123
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: make sure that a variety of API server requests are retried during "init", "join", "upgrade", "reset" workflows. Prior to this change some API server requests, such as, creating or updating ConfigMaps were "one-shot" - i.e. they could fail if the API server dropped connectivity for a very short period of time.

enrichment.problem: During kubeadm init, join, upgrade, and reset workflows, certain API server requests (e.g., creating or updating ConfigMaps) were executed as one‑shot operations. A brief loss of connectivity to the API server could cause those requests to fail, aborting the workflow.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm commands (init, join, upgrade, reset) on clusters, especially in environments where the API server may experience short‑lived connectivity interruptions.
enrichment.fix: Added retry logic in kubeadm for a variety of API server calls, ensuring that transient connectivity glitches are retried until they succeed.
enrichment.impact: kubeadm bootstrapping and lifecycle operations become more resilient; clusters are less likely to fail to initialize, join, upgrade, or reset due to temporary API server outages.

other.description: Updated kubedns and nodelocaldns to version `v1.23.0`.
other.author: bzsuni
other.userFacingChange: Update kubedns and nodelocaldns to v1.23.0

enrichment.problem: Clusters were using older versions of the kube-dns and node-local-dns add‑ons, which may lack recent bug fixes, security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that runs the kube-dns or node‑local‑dns add‑on; pods and services that rely on cluster DNS resolution.
enrichment.fix: The add‑ons are upgraded to version v1.23.0, bringing the latest upstream changes into the cluster.
enrichment.impact: Users benefit from more stable and secure DNS resolution for pods and nodes, and can take advantage of performance and feature enhancements included in v1.23.0.

other.description: "`NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature is now GA."
other.author: jsafrane
other.userFacingChange: NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature is now GA.

enrichment.problem: Clusters had only an alpha/beta implementation of volume reconstruction, requiring a feature gate and lacking production‑grade stability, which made pod recovery after node restarts unreliable.
enrichment.affected: Any workload using CSI PersistentVolumes that may experience node restarts or failures; cluster operators no longer need to enable a feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature is promoted to GA. The feature gate is removed and the reconstruction logic is enabled by default in kubelet, with additional testing and hardening.
enrichment.impact: Pods with CSI PersistentVolumes now automatically reconstruct their volumes after a node reboot or failure without extra configuration, increasing reliability and reducing operational overhead.

other.description: kubeadm: the `bridge-nf-call-iptables=1` and `bridge-nf-call-ip6tables=1` preflight checks are removed since not all the network implementations require this setting, network plugins are responsible for setting this correctly depending on whether or not they connect containers to Linux bridges or use some other mechanism.
other.author: SataQiu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: the bridge-nf-call-iptables=1 and bridge-nf-call-ip6tables=1 preflight checks are removed since not all the network implementations require this setting, network plugins are responsible for setting this correctly depending on whether or not they connect containers to Linux bridges or use some other mechanism.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm preflight checks required bridge-nf-call-iptables=1 and bridge-nf-call-ip6tables=1 sysctl settings, causing initialization failures for network plugins that do not use Linux bridges.
enrichment.affected: Users initializing or joining clusters with kubeadm using network plugins that do not rely on Linux bridges (e.g., many CNI implementations).
enrichment.fix: Removed the bridge-nf-call-iptables and bridge-nf-call-ip6tables preflight checks from kubeadm. Network plugins are now responsible for setting these sysctls if needed.
enrichment.impact: Cluster setup with kubeadm no longer fails for CNI plugins that don’t need bridge sysctls, simplifying deployment and reducing unnecessary configuration steps. Users must ensure the sysctls are set appropriately for plugins that require them.

other.description: "Upgraded metrics server to `v0.7.0`."
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: upgrade metrics server to v0.7.0

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or controllers that query the metrics‑server (e.g., HPA, custom metrics consumers) will see the updated server behavior.
enrichment.fix: Upgraded the metrics-server addon to version v0.7.0.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will run the newer metrics‑server release which includes bug fixes, additional metric APIs, and performance improvements. Components that depend on pod metrics, such as the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, will receive more accurate and reliable data.

other.description: "Accepted zero as a default value for `kubectl create` token duration."
other.author: ah8ad3
other.userFacingChange: Accept zero as a default value for kubectl create token duration

enrichment.problem: kubectl create token previously rejected a duration value of zero, preventing users from generating tokens with no expiry or using zero as the default.
enrichment.affected: Users invoking `kubectl create token` who need a token with zero (unlimited) duration.
enrichment.fix: The command now accepts zero as a valid default value for the token duration flag, allowing unlimited‑lifetime tokens or explicitly setting a zero duration.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can create non‑expiring service account tokens without extra workarounds, improving usability of token generation.

other.description: Reverted the change to "support sharing waitingPods across different scheduler profiles".
other.author: kerthcet
other.userFacingChange: Revert "support sharing waitingPods across different scheduler profiles"

issueContext.title: Flake: TestFrameworkHandler_IterateOverWaitingPods/pods_with_different_profiles_are_waiting_on_permit_stage [46c1b1ee...]

enrichment.problem: A recent change that allowed sharing waitingPods across different scheduler profiles caused a flaky test (TestFrameworkHandler_IterateOverWaitingPods) where pods with different profiles were incorrectly waiting on the permit stage.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using multiple scheduler profiles could experience incorrect pod queuing; primarily affects the scheduler component and its test suite.
enrichment.fix: The change has been reverted, restoring the original behavior where waitingPods are not shared across scheduler profiles, thereby fixing the test flake and preventing incorrect cross‑profile pod waiting.
enrichment.impact: CI pipelines and developers no longer see the flaky test failure; scheduler behavior returns to the stable, expected handling of waiting pods per profile, avoiding potential mis‑scheduling in multi‑profile setups.

other.description: Renamed Label cluster to `storage_cluster_id` for `apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric`
other.author: dims
other.userFacingChange: For apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, we are renaming the label for etcd to be "storage_cluster_id" instead of "cluster" to to reduce conflict and be very specific.

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric used the generic label "cluster" for etcd, which could conflict with other metrics and was not specific enough for users.
enrichment.affected: Clusters collecting the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, especially users with Prometheus alerts or dashboards that reference the "cluster" label.
enrichment.fix: Renamed the label to "storage_cluster_id", making it unique and clearly indicating that it identifies the storage cluster associated with the metric.
enrichment.impact: Improves metric clarity and avoids label collisions, helping monitoring setups (e.g., Prometheus) and dashboards to correctly attribute storage size data without ambiguity.

other.description: Bumped the stability level of apiserver_storage_size_bytes to `STABLE`
other.author: logicalhan
other.userFacingChange:
```release-note
NONE
```

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric was previously marked as beta/unstable, so users could not rely on it for production monitoring or alerting.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that monitor the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric for API server storage usage; alerts and dashboards built on this metric.
enrichment.fix: Its stability level was promoted to STABLE, signalling guaranteed API compatibility and ongoing support.
enrichment.impact: Operators and monitoring tools can now safely use this metric in dashboards and alerts without fearing breakage, improving reliability of storage‑related observability for the API server.

deprecation.description: The deprecated `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, which has been deprecated since `v1.27`, has been removed. It is recommended to use the Pod Security Admission plugin instead, which has been available since v1.25. Refer to the [Kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#securitycontextdeny) for more information.
deprecation.author: mtardy
deprecation.userFacingChange: Removed the `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, deprecated since v1.27. The [Pod Security Admission](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-admission/) plugin, available since v1.25, is recommended instead.

enrichment.problem: The `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin, deprecated since v1.27, was removed, causing clusters that still have the plugin enabled to fail pod creation or encounter configuration errors.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that have the `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin enabled; cluster administrators and workloads that rely on that plugin for pod security validation.
enrichment.fix: The plugin has been removed from the codebase. Administrators should migrate to the newer Pod Security Admission plugin (available since v1.25) to enforce security policies.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with `SecurityContextDeny` enabled must update their admission controller configuration; otherwise pod creation will be blocked. The change streamlines security controls by consolidating enforcement under Pod Security Admission.

apiChange.description: Fixes a 1.30.0 regression in openapi descriptions of imagePullSecrets and hostAliases fields to mark the fields used as keys in those lists as either defaulted or required.
apiChange.author: pmalek

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.30.0 caused the OpenAPI schema for the pod fields imagePullSecrets and hostAliases to omit proper markings for the key fields, so they were not indicated as defaulted or required. This led to inaccurate client code generation and validation for these fields.
enrichment.affected: Developers and tooling that consume the OpenAPI specifications for pod specifications, especially when using imagePullSecrets or hostAliases. This includes custom clients, client-go code generation, and kubectl validation.
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI descriptions for imagePullSecrets and hostAliases have been updated to correctly mark the key fields as either defaulted or required, restoring the expected schema behavior.
enrichment.impact: Clients, code generators, and tools that rely on the OpenAPI schema (e.g., kubectl, client-go generators) now receive accurate field metadata, preventing mis‑generated code or validation errors when using imagePullSecrets or hostAliases in pod specs.

apiChange.description: Fixes a 1.30.0 regression in openapi descriptions of imagePullSecrets and hostAliases fields to mark the fields used as keys in those lists as either defaulted or required.
apiChange.author: pmalek

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.30.0 caused the OpenAPI v2/v3 schemas for the pod spec fields `imagePullSecrets` and `hostAliases` to omit the `defaulted` or `required` markers for the key fields within those lists. This led to inaccurate API documentation and broke client‑generation tools or validation that rely on correct OpenAPI metadata.
enrichment.affected: Any tooling or users that depend on the Kubernetes OpenAPI specifications for `imagePullSecrets` or `hostAliases` (e.g., client libraries, kubectl, validation webhooks).
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI generation logic was updated to correctly mark the key fields of `imagePullSecrets` and `hostAliases` as either defaulted or required, restoring the proper schema definitions.
enrichment.impact: Clients, code generators, and validation tools that consume the Kubernetes OpenAPI spec now receive accurate information about required keys, preventing generation bugs and ensuring correct API usage.

bugOrRegression.description: Expose --applyconfig-openapi-schema flag for client generation and fix applyconfig-gen to not create import cycles
bugOrRegression.author: soltysh

enrichment.problem: The applyconfig-gen tool created import cycles during client generation, and the --applyconfig-openapi-schema flag was not exposed, preventing users from generating correct ApplyConfiguration client code.
enrichment.affected: Users of the client-go code generation tooling (applyconfig-gen) who need to generate ApplyConfiguration clients.
enrichment.fix: A new --applyconfig-openapi-schema flag is now exposed for client generation, and applyconfig-gen has been corrected to avoid creating import cycles.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now generate client-go ApplyConfiguration code without build failures, improving developer workflow and enabling proper use of the server‑side apply feature.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix throughput when scheduling daemonset pods to reach 300 pods/s, if the configured qps allows it.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler could not achieve high scheduling rates for DaemonSet pods, falling short of the expected 300 pods per second even when the QPS configuration allowed it.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run DaemonSets with many pods, especially when administrators have increased the scheduler QPS setting.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler logic was updated to remove the bottleneck limiting DaemonSet pod scheduling, enabling the scheduler to reach up to 300 pods/s when the configured QPS permits.
enrichment.impact: Large DaemonSets (e.g., monitoring agents, log collectors) can now be rolled out or scaled much faster, reducing rollout time and improving cluster responsiveness during high‑scale DaemonSet operations.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin refusing in-tree Azure Disk and vSphere PersistentVolumes.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: The PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin incorrectly rejected PersistentVolume objects for the in‑tree Azure Disk and vSphere storage providers, preventing their creation.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use in‑tree Azure Disk or vSphere PersistentVolumes were unable to create those volumes. The issue affected any workload that relied on those storage types.
enrichment.fix: The admission plugin logic was updated to recognize and allow Azure Disk and vSphere in‑tree PersistentVolumes, so they are no longer denied.
enrichment.impact: Users can now create and bind Azure Disk and vSphere PersistentVolumes without errors, restoring expected storage functionality for those workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.29.0 regression that introduced a possible data race that could cause panics in kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in v1.29.0 caused a data race in the kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler, which could lead to panics and crashes of these control‑plane components.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded to v1.29.0 that run the kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler could experience crashes under load.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected by eliminating the unsafe concurrent access, removing the data race and ensuring the affected code paths are properly synchronized.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unexpected panics in the controller manager and scheduler, preserving cluster stability and avoiding control‑plane outages for users running v1.29.0.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: during the preflight check "CreateJob" of "kubeadm upgrade", check if there are no nodes where a Pod can schedule. If there are none, show a warning and skip this preflight check. This can happen in single node clusters where the only node was drained.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: During "kubeadm upgrade", the preflight check that creates a Job fails when no node in the cluster can schedule a pod. In single‑node clusters where the sole node has been drained, this causes the upgrade to abort with an error.
enrichment.affected: Operators performing a kubeadm upgrade on single‑node clusters (or any cluster where all nodes are drained) where the upgrade previously failed due to the CreateJob preflight check.
enrichment.fix: The preflight check now detects the situation where zero nodes are eligible to run a pod, emits a warning, and skips the CreateJob check instead of treating it as a failure.
enrichment.impact: Allows kubeadm upgrades to succeed in single‑node (or otherwise fully‑drained) clusters, removing a false‑positive failure and reducing operational friction for operators.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a regression where the KubeletConfiguration is not properly downloaded during "kubeadm upgrade" commands from the kube-system/kubelet-config ConfigMap, resulting in the local '/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml' file being written as a defaulted config.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: During "kubeadm upgrade" the kubelet configuration was not fetched from the kube-system/kubelet-config ConfigMap, causing /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml to be overwritten with a default configuration.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded with kubeadm that rely on a custom KubeletConfiguration stored in the kube-system/kubelet-config ConfigMap.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now correctly downloads the KubeletConfiguration from the kubelet-config ConfigMap during upgrade commands, ensuring the existing custom kubelet config is preserved.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use a custom KubeletConfiguration managed via the kubelet-config ConfigMap will retain their intended settings after an upgrade, preventing unexpected changes to node behavior, performance, or security posture.

apiChange.description: Added the feature gates `StrictCostEnforcementForVAP` and `StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks` to enforce the strct cost calculation for CEL extended libraries. It is strongly recommended to turn on the feature gates as early as possible.
apiChange.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: Cost calculations for CEL extended libraries used in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and admission webhooks were not strictly enforced, potentially allowing inaccurate resource accounting and unintended admission of workloads.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or admission webhooks with CEL expressions could see more accurate cost enforcement once the feature gates are enabled.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two feature gates, StrictCostEnforcementForVAP and StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks, which when enabled enforce strict cost calculation for CEL extended libraries during admission processing.
enrichment.impact: Ensures more reliable and safe admission decisions by preventing under‑estimation of resource costs, helping clusters avoid over‑commitment and maintain consistent policy enforcement.

apiChange.description:
Improved scheduling performance when many nodes, and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset)
  For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
apiChange.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: Scheduling was slow in large clusters when the prefilter phase filtered down to only a few nodes (e.g., daemonset workloads). Additionally, the meaning of missing entries in the NodeToStatusMap for out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins was unclear.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many nodes and workloads that rely on daemonsets or custom PostFilter plugins. Plugin developers need to adjust code for the changed NodeToStatusMap semantics.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler code was optimized to speed up the scheduling path when prefilter returns only 1‑2 candidate nodes. The semantics of NodeToStatusMap were clarified: a node absent from the map is now treated as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status, so PostFilter plugins must handle this case explicitly.
enrichment.impact: Large clusters see noticeably faster pod scheduling, especially for daemonset pods. Plugin developers must update their PostFilter implementations to account for the new default status, preventing unexpected scheduling decisions.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.3
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Not applicable – the change is a tooling update rather than a bug or missing capability.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that are built from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) and any CI/CD pipelines that compile Kubernetes.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes binaries are now built with the Go 1.22.3 toolchain instead of the previous Go version.
enrichment.impact: Allows Kubernetes to benefit from Go 1.22.3 security patches, performance improvements, and language features; ensures CI/CD pipelines and downstream builds can use the same version, reducing build inconsistencies.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.4
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go compiler version, which could cause build failures, lack of recent language/security updates, and incompatibility with newer tooling.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including CI/CD pipelines, release engineers, and downstream distributors.
enrichment.fix: The source tree is now compiled with Go 1.22.4, updating the toolchain used for all builds and CI pipelines.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI systems building Kubernetes will have a supported, up‑to‑date compiler, reducing build‑time issues and gaining Go security and performance improvements. No runtime behavior for clusters changes.

bugOrRegression.description: Drop additional rule requirement (cronjobs/finalizers) in the roles who use kubectl create cronjobs to be backwards compatible
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: Roles that used `kubectl create cronjob` were required to include an extra RBAC rule for `cronjobs/finalizers`. This broke existing roles that did not have that rule, causing cronjob creation to fail after the change.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where administrators granted roles for `kubectl create cronjob` but omitted the `cronjobs/finalizers` permission. The issue manifested as authorization failures when creating CronJobs.
enrichment.fix: The additional rule requirement for `cronjobs/finalizers` has been removed from the RBAC checks performed by `kubectl create cronjobs`, restoring backwards compatibility.
enrichment.impact: Users can now create CronJobs with existing RBAC roles without adding new permissions, preventing unexpected authorization errors during upgrades and simplifying role definitions.

bugOrRegression.description: Emition of RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events has been removed from stateful set lifecycle.
bugOrRegression.author: atiratree

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet controller emitted RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events, which were rarely used and could cause confusion for users watching pod lifecycle events.
enrichment.affected: Any automation, monitoring, or alerting that relied on the RecreatingFailedPod or RecreatingTerminatedPod events will no longer see them.
enrichment.fix: The emission of these two events has been removed from the StatefulSet lifecycle logic, so they will no longer be generated.
enrichment.impact: Users or tools that depended on these events will stop receiving them, requiring updates to monitoring or automation that listened for these specific event types. No functional change to StatefulSet behavior otherwise.

bugOrRegression.description: Improved scheduling latency when many gated pods
bugOrRegression.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: When a large number of gated (pending) pods are present, the kube‑scheduler experiences high latency, delaying pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that create or maintain a high count of gated (pending) pods, such as those using admission gating, batch jobs, or custom controllers that temporarily block pods.
enrichment.fix: Optimized the scheduler’s handling of gated pods, reducing the time spent in the scheduling loop and improving overall scheduling latency.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with many pending/gated pods will schedule pods faster, leading to quicker workload start‑up and better resource utilization.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.28 regression printing pods with invalid initContainer status
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.28 the apiserver regressed and would display pods with an invalid initContainer status, leading to confusing or incorrect pod status output for users.
enrichment.affected: Any workflow or tool that retrieves pod status, especially those with initContainers, could see incorrect status information.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver printing logic was corrected to properly handle and omit invalid initContainer status entries, restoring accurate pod status representations.
enrichment.impact: Users querying pod status (e.g., via kubectl) now see correct information, avoiding misinterpretation of pod health and reducing support tickets.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-scheduler: fixes a 1.30 regression that can lead to a scheduler crash when processing pods with affinity that doesn't match a real/valid node
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: Kube-scheduler could crash when processing pods that specify node affinity rules that do not match any real or valid node, a regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.30.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded to 1.30 that have pods with node affinity rules pointing to non‑existent nodes; the scheduler would crash, halting pod placement.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was corrected to safely handle invalid affinity specifications, preventing a panic and ensuring the scheduler continues running.
enrichment.impact: Stops cluster-wide scheduling failures and downtime after upgrading to 1.30, protecting workloads that use affinity—even when mis‑configured or referencing nodes that no longer exist.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: during kubelet health checks, respect the healthz address:port configured in the KubeletConfiguration instead of hardcoding localhost:10248.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm's kubelet health checks always used the hardcoded address localhost:10248, ignoring any custom healthz address:port set in the KubeletConfiguration. This caused health checks to fail when the kubelet was configured to listen on a different address or port.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with a non‑default kubelet healthz address or port, typically users customizing kubelet configuration for security or networking reasons.
enrichment.fix: The health check logic was updated to read and use the healthz address and port from the KubeletConfiguration, allowing kubeadm to correctly probe the kubelet's health endpoint regardless of custom settings.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that customize the kubelet health endpoint will now be correctly identified as healthy during bootstrap and ongoing health checks, preventing false‑negative health reports and potential node join failures.

securityFixes.title: Incorrect permissions on Windows containers logs
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes clusters with Windows nodes
where BUILTIN\Users may be able to read container logs and NT
AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users may be able to modify container logs.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were compiled with an older Go version; the release needed to update the toolchain.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) built from source.
enrichment.fix: The build process is updated to use Go 1.22.5 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: Provides up‑to‑date language runtime improvements, security patches, and performance enhancements to all Kubernetes binaries, benefiting every cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Add `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` to default masked paths. It avoids the potential security risk that the ability to read these files may offer a power-based sidechannel attack against any workloads running on the same kernel.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: Containers could read files under /sys/devices/virtual/powercap, exposing power consumption data that could be used for side‑channel attacks against other workloads on the same node.
enrichment.affected: Pods running on the same node could be targeted by malicious containers that read powercap information; the change protects all workloads on nodes managed by kubelet.
enrichment.fix: The path /sys/devices/virtual/powercap is added to the kubelet's default masked paths, automatically hiding these files from containers.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface of nodes by preventing potential cross‑tenant power‑based side‑channel attacks, improving tenant isolation and overall cluster security.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix a bug that Pods could stuck in the unschedulable pod pool 
  if they're rejected by PreEnqueue plugins that could change its result by a change in resources apart from Pods.
  DRA plugin is the only plugin that meets the criteria of the bug in in-tree, 
  and hence if you have `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature flag enabled, 
  your DRA Pods could be affected by this bug.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: Pods could become permanently stuck in the unschedulable pod pool when rejected by PreEnqueue plugins that later change their result due to external resource changes. In-tree, only the DynamicResourceAllocation (DRA) plugin exhibits this behavior, so DRA-enabled Pods could remain unschedulable indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Users with the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate enabled and DRA Pods that rely on the scheduler's PreEnqueue plugins.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler's handling of PreEnqueue plugin rejections has been corrected so that Pods are no longer left in the unschedulable pool after resource changes, allowing them to be re‑evaluated and scheduled properly.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that workloads using the DynamicResourceAllocation feature can be scheduled reliably, preventing silent pod starvation and improving overall cluster stability for those users.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix endpoints status out-of-sync when the pod state changes rapidly
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: When a pod transitioned rapidly between states (e.g., quickly becoming Ready then NotReady), the Endpoints controller could leave the Service endpoint list out of sync, causing stale or missing endpoint entries.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on Services/Endpoints for traffic routing, especially those with fast pod restarts such as Deployments, Jobs, or CI/CD pipelines.
enrichment.fix: The Endpoints controller in kube‑controller‑manager now correctly updates endpoint status even under rapid pod state changes, ensuring the endpoint list reflects the current pod readiness.
enrichment.impact: Services always route traffic to pods that are truly Ready, preventing requests from being sent to terminated or NotReady pods. This improves reliability for workloads that perform fast rollouts, Job restarts, or any rapid pod lifecycle events.

bugOrRegression.description:
For statically provisioned PVs, if its volume source is CSI type or it has migrated annotation, when it's deleted, the PersisentVolume controller won't changes its phase to the Failed state. 
  With this patch, the external provisioner can remove the finalizer in next reconcile loop. Unfortunately if the provious existing pv has the Failed state, this patch won't take effort. It requires users to remove finalizer.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When a statically provisioned PersistentVolume with a CSI volume source or the migrated annotation is deleted, the PersistentVolume controller fails to set its phase to Failed, preventing the external provisioner from removing the finalizer.
enrichment.affected: Users with statically provisioned PVs that use CSI drivers or have the migrated annotation; clusters that rely on external provisioners to delete such PVs.
enrichment.fix: The controller now updates the PV's phase to Failed during deletion, enabling the external provisioner to clear the finalizer in the next reconcile loop. Existing PVs already in Failed state still require manual finalizer removal.
enrichment.impact: Ensures proper cleanup of CSI‑based static PVs, avoiding stuck finalizers and potential storage resource leaks, improving reliability of volume lifecycle management.

bugOrRegression.description: Job: Fix a bug that the SuccessCriteriaMet could be added to the Job with successPolicy regardless of the featureGate enabling
bugOrRegression.author: tenzen-y

enrichment.problem: The Job API allowed the `SuccessCriteriaMet` condition to be added when a `successPolicy` was specified, even if the corresponding feature gate was disabled. This bypassed the intended gating logic.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing Job resources could see the `successPolicy` take effect even when the feature gate was off, leading to confusing job outcomes.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic now correctly checks the feature gate before accepting `successPolicy`/`SuccessCriteriaMet` fields for Jobs, preventing them from being added when the feature is disabled.
enrichment.impact: Prevents jobs from silently using the success policy feature when it is not enabled, avoiding unexpected job behavior and ensuring feature‑gate semantics are respected.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: cji

enrichment.problem: Not specified (release note missing)
enrichment.affected: Not specified (release note missing)
enrichment.fix: Not specified (release note missing)
enrichment.impact: Not specified (release note missing)

apiChange.description: Fixed a bug in the API server where empty collections of ValidatingAdmissionPolicies did not have an `items` field.
apiChange.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: When the API server returned an empty list of ValidatingAdmissionPolicies, the response omitted the required `items` field, causing client parsers to error on list operations.
enrichment.affected: Any component or user that queries the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API and expects a standard list response, especially when no policies are defined.
enrichment.fix: The API server was updated to always include an `items` array (empty when no policies exist) in the list response for ValidatingAdmissionPolicies.
enrichment.impact: Clients and tools that list ValidatingAdmissionPolicies—such as kubectl, controllers, and automated pipelines—can now reliably handle empty results without crashes or parsing errors.

apiChange.description: Use omitempty for optional Job Pod Failure Policy fields
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Optional fields in the Job podFailurePolicy were always serialized, leading to empty fields appearing in Job specifications and API responses.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing Job resources that include (or omit) podFailurePolicy fields. Controllers and clients that read Job specs will see a more concise representation.
enrichment.fix: The API serialization now uses `omitempty` for these optional podFailurePolicy fields, so they are omitted when not set.
enrichment.impact: Job objects are cleaner and smaller in etcd and API responses, reducing confusion for users and downstream tools that parse Job specs.

bugOrRegression.description: Disabled a previously on-by-default optimization for the API server where each **watch** response used a dedicated goroutine. The `APIServingWithRoutine` feature gate has been demoted from beta to alpha, and is now off by default.
bugOrRegression.author: benluddy

enrichment.problem: The API server had an on‑by‑default optimization that created a dedicated goroutine for each watch response, which could consume excessive goroutine, CPU, and memory resources in clusters with many watches.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run many watch clients against the API server, especially those that previously benefited from the per‑watch‑response goroutine optimization.
enrichment.fix: The optimization is now disabled by default. The APIServingWithRoutine feature gate is demoted from beta to alpha and turned off, so watches no longer get a per‑response goroutine unless the gate is manually enabled.
enrichment.impact: Reduces goroutine count and resource usage on the API server, improving stability for large numbers of watches. Watch latency may be slightly higher for users who relied on the optimization, but the behavior can be restored by enabling the feature gate.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix the bug where PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When a pod reached a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed), the PodIP field was removed from the pod status temporarily, causing consumers that still read the IP (e.g., monitoring, logging, or cleanup scripts) to encounter missing data or errors.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that runs to completion (Jobs, Pods with restartPolicy=Never, etc.) and any component or script that reads the PodIP after the pod has terminated.
enrichment.fix: The pod status handling was updated so that the PodIP field is retained even after the pod becomes terminal, ensuring the IP address remains available throughout the pod's lifecycle.
enrichment.impact: Tools and controllers that rely on a pod's IP after completion can now retrieve it reliably, preventing failures in post‑completion processing and improving observability of pod lifecycles.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that init containers with `Always` restartPolicy may not terminate gracefully if the pod hasn't initialized yet.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: Init containers configured with restartPolicy=Always could fail to terminate gracefully when the pod had not yet completed its initialization phase, causing the pod to hang.
enrichment.affected: Pods using init containers with restartPolicy=Always, especially during early pod initialization.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now correctly handles termination of Always‑restart init containers even before the pod is fully initialized, ensuring graceful shutdown.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers with an Always restart policy will start and stop reliably, preventing stuck init containers and improving overall workload stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression watching a single namespace via the deprecated /api/v1/watch/namespaces/$name endpoint where watch events were not delivered after the watch was established
bugOrRegression.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: When using the deprecated `/api/v1/watch/namespaces/<name>` endpoint to watch a single namespace (available from v1.27 onward), the kube-apiserver established the watch but failed to deliver any subsequent watch events.
enrichment.affected: Clients that use the deprecated single‑namespace watch endpoint (e.g., custom controllers, operators, and scripts) could miss events after the watch was set up.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑apiserver watch implementation was corrected so that events are now correctly streamed after the watch is established for the single‑namespace endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, operators, and client applications that rely on namespace‑specific watches will once again receive accurate event streams, preventing missed updates and ensuring correct reconciliation logic.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a potential crash serving CustomResourceDefinitions that combine an invalid schema and CEL validation rules.
bugOrRegression.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver could panic and crash when serving CustomResourceDefinitions that specified an invalid OpenAPI schema combined with CEL validation rules, causing API unavailability for those resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have CustomResourceDefinitions containing both an invalid schema and CEL validation rules. Controllers, operators, and kubectl commands that interact with such CRDs were at risk of causing an apiserver crash.
enrichment.fix: Adds validation and safeguards in the apiserver to detect the invalid schema + CEL combination early and handle it gracefully, preventing a server crash.
enrichment.impact: Ensures the API server remains stable and continues to serve all APIs, protecting clusters that use CRDs with CEL validation from unexpected downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: Added `--yes` flag to the list of allowed flags so that it can be mixed with `kubeadm upgrade apply --config`
bugOrRegression.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: When running `kubeadm upgrade apply --config`, the `--yes` flag was not recognized, preventing users from automatically confirming prompts during upgrades.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using `kubeadm upgrade apply` with a configuration file and who want to skip interactive confirmation.
enrichment.fix: The `--yes` flag is now added to the whitelist of allowed flags for `kubeadm upgrade apply`, allowing it to be used together with `--config`.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can perform non‑interactive, scripted upgrades with a configuration file, simplifying automation and reducing manual steps.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed a bug on 'kubeadm join' where using patches with a kubeletconfiguration target was not respected when performing the local kubelet healthz check.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When using `kubeadm join` with patches that target a KubeletConfiguration, the patches were ignored during the local kubelet healthz check, potentially causing the join to fail or use incorrect kubelet settings.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where nodes are added using `kubeadm join` with `--patches` that modify KubeletConfiguration. Affects administrators performing node joins and the kubelet on the joining node.
enrichment.fix: The join workflow now correctly applies patches targeting KubeletConfiguration before performing the local kubelet healthz probe, ensuring the kubelet runs with the intended configuration.
enrichment.impact: Users joining nodes with custom kubelet configuration patches can now rely on a successful join and proper kubelet behavior, eliminating join failures caused by ignored patches.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed a regression where the JoinConfiguration.discovery.timeout was no longer respected and the value was always hardcoded to "5m" (5 minutes).
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm ignored the user‑specified JoinConfiguration.discovery.timeout and always used a hard‑coded 5‑minute timeout, causing joins to fail or hang when the discovery phase took longer than 5 minutes.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm join with a non‑default discovery timeout was affected; the join would always fall back to 5 minutes regardless of the configured value.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed so that the timeout value provided in JoinConfiguration.discovery.timeout is now correctly applied during kubeadm join operations.
enrichment.impact: Users can once again rely on custom discovery timeouts, preventing premature join failures in slow networks or large clusters and improving the reliability of kubeadm joins.

bugOrRegression.description: Mount-utils: treat syscall.ENODEV as corrupted mount
bugOrRegression.author: dobsonj

enrichment.problem: Mount utilities did not treat syscall.ENODEV errors as indicating a corrupted mount, so stale or broken mounts were not cleaned up, leading to mount failures or hanging pods.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running the kubelet and any pods that use volume mounts; especially workloads that encounter device removal or mount corruption.
enrichment.fix: The mount-utils code now interprets ENODEV as a sign of a corrupted mount and triggers the appropriate cleanup/recovery logic.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of volume mounts on nodes, preventing pods from being stuck in a pending or error state due to unhandled mount corruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolve a regression in 1.30 default behavior for kubectl exec, cp, and attach which fail when using an HTTPS proxy.
bugOrRegression.author: seans3

enrichment.problem: kubectl exec, cp, and attach commands fail when an HTTPS proxy is configured, regressing the default behavior introduced in v1.30.
enrichment.affected: Developers and operators who run kubectl exec, cp, or attach from environments that use an HTTPS proxy.
enrichment.fix: Restored the correct handling of HTTPS proxies in the kubectl client, ensuring exec, cp, and attach work as expected even when a proxy is set.
enrichment.impact: Users who rely on these commands for debugging or file transfer while operating behind an HTTPS proxy can now use them without errors, reducing workflow interruptions and avoiding the need to unset proxy settings.

bugOrRegression.description: StatefulSet autodelete will respect controlling owners on PVC claims as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4375
bugOrRegression.author: mattcary

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet pod auto‑deletion could remove PersistentVolumeClaims even when those claims had other controlling owners, leading to unintended PVC deletion and possible data loss.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets that create PVCs which may also be referenced by other resources (e.g., snapshots, backups, or custom controllers).
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSet controller now checks the controlling owners of a PVC before deleting it during pod auto‑deletion, and only deletes the claim if it is not owned by any other resource.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental loss of persistent data for workloads that use StatefulSets with shared or secondary owners of PVCs, making PVC lifecycle management safer and more predictable.

bugOrRegression.description: Stop using wmic on Windows to get uuid in the kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: The kubelet on Windows used the `wmic` command to retrieve the machine UUID. In newer Windows environments `wmic` is deprecated or may fail, causing the kubelet to be unable to obtain a reliable node identifier.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run Windows worker nodes with the kubelet. The issue manifested as kubelet start‑up failures or incorrect node identity on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The code path that called `wmic` has been removed and replaced with a supported method for retrieving the UUID on Windows, eliminating the dependency on `wmic`.
enrichment.impact: Windows nodes can now reliably acquire a UUID during kubelet startup, preventing node registration or identity‑related errors and improving cluster stability for mixed OS clusters.

apiChange.description: Fixes a regression in openapi descriptions of PodIP.IP  and HostIP.IP fields to mark the fields used as keys in those lists as required.
apiChange.author: thockin

enrichment.problem: A regression caused the OpenAPI schema for PodIP.IP and HostIP.IP fields to omit the required marker on the key fields, breaking client code generation and validation that expects these fields to be required.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that consume the Kubernetes OpenAPI spec (e.g., client libraries, code generators) were affected because the spec incorrectly marked required fields.
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI descriptions for PodIP.IP and HostIP.IP have been updated to correctly mark the key fields as required.
enrichment.impact: Clients and tools that rely on the OpenAPI spec will correctly treat PodIP and HostIP as required fields again, preventing validation errors and ensuring generated code works as expected.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go compiler, which may lack recent security fixes, performance improvements, and language features.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and clusters that run the newly built binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile the entire codebase with Go 1.22.6.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) gain the benefits of the newer Go version, including security patches and runtime improvements, without changing runtime behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a scheduler preemption issue where the victim pod was not deleted due to incorrect status patching. This issue occurred when the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes in their status, causing the preemption to fail entirely.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: When the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes, the scheduler patched the victim pod's status incorrectly, so the victim pod was not deleted and preemption failed completely.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on scheduler preemption, especially when the preemptor and victim pods belong to different QoS classes.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now correctly updates the victim pod's status regardless of QoS class differences, ensuring the victim pod is deleted and preemption proceeds as expected.
enrichment.impact: Preemption works across QoS classes again, preventing scheduling dead‑locks and allowing higher‑priority pods to be scheduled when lower‑priority pods need to be evicted.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix race condition in kube-proxy initialization that could blackhole UDP traffic to service VIP.
bugOrRegression.author: wedaly

enrichment.problem: A race condition during kube-proxy initialization could leave UDP service IPVS/iptables rules incomplete, causing UDP packets to be silently dropped (blackholed) for services using a virtual IP.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy with UDP services; pods receiving traffic via a Service VIP could have experienced blackholed UDP packets.
enrichment.fix: The initialization sequence in kube-proxy was re‑ordered and synchronized so that the service rules are fully installed before traffic is allowed, eliminating the race condition.
enrichment.impact: UDP‑based services (e.g., DNS, video streaming, custom protocols) will no longer experience intermittent loss of traffic during kube-proxy startup, improving reliability for workloads that depend on UDP.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that doesn't allow to install k8s.io/kube-openapi dependency on execute kube::codegen::gen_openapi.
bugOrRegression.author: kannon92

enrichment.problem: Running the kube::codegen::gen_openapi command failed because the k8s.io/kube-openapi Go module could not be installed, breaking OpenAPI generation.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes developers and CI jobs that run the API code generation tooling were unable to generate OpenAPI specs.
enrichment.fix: The code generation script was updated to correctly allow the k8s.io/kube-openapi dependency to be installed, enabling successful execution of gen_openapi.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines that generate OpenAPI specs for Kubernetes APIs can now build without errors, restoring a critical part of the API development workflow.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: Init containers could fail to start when the container runtime experienced a temporary failure, causing pod startup errors.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use init containers; any workload that depends on successful init container execution could be delayed or fail.
enrichment.fix: Added logic to handle transient container runtime failures during init container startup, allowing the kubelet to retry and successfully start the init containers once the runtime recovers.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of pod initialization by preventing unnecessary init container crashes, reducing pod startup latency and avoiding failures for workloads that rely on init containers.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a regression in 1.29+ default configurations, where regular init containers may fail to start due to a temporary container runtime failure.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in the default configuration for Kubernetes 1.29+ caused regular init containers to fail to start when the container runtime temporarily failed, leading to pod startup failures.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses init containers on clusters upgraded to or created with Kubernetes 1.29+ default settings; the issue manifested on nodes where the container runtime experienced temporary failures.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by correcting the default configuration handling of transient container runtime errors, ensuring init containers are retried and can start successfully.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use init containers now start reliably, preventing unnecessary pod failures and reducing operational disruptions for workloads that depend on init containers.

bugOrRegression.description: Terminated Pods on a node will not be re-admitted on kubelet restart. This fixes the problem of Completed Pods awaiting for the finalizer marked as Failed after the kubelet restart.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: After a kubelet restart, pods that had already terminated were not re-admitted and remained pending finalization, causing them to be marked as Failed.
enrichment.affected: Pods that have completed on a node where the kubelet is restarted; primarily affects workloads relying on accurate pod termination status.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now correctly re-admits terminated pods on restart, allowing any pending finalizers to complete and preventing the pods from being incorrectly marked Failed.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that completed pods (e.g., from Jobs) maintain the correct lifecycle status after a node reboot or kubelet restart, avoiding false failure reports and simplifying troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description: Upgrade coreDNS to v1.11.3
bugOrRegression.author: BenTheElder

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that uses the CoreDNS addon; all workloads that rely on DNS for service discovery.
enrichment.fix: CoreDNS addon is upgraded to version v1.11.3.
enrichment.impact: Clusters will run a newer CoreDNS version that includes bug fixes, performance improvements, and security patches, ensuring more reliable DNS resolution for all pods and services.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.7
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: No functional issue; this change updates the Go compiler version used to build Kubernetes binaries from older Go versions to Go 1.22.7.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that are compiled from source are affected, as they are now built with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process now compiles all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.7, incorporating upstream Go runtime bug fixes, performance improvements, and security patches.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kubelet, kube-apiserver, scheduler, controller‑manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) benefit from the newer Go toolchain, improving runtime stability and future compatibility without changing cluster behavior.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.8
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: No functional problem; this change updates the Kubernetes build process to use Go version 1.22.8 instead of the previous Go version.
enrichment.affected: Developers building Kubernetes from source, CI pipelines, and any downstream projects that depend on the Kubernetes build artifacts.
enrichment.fix: The build system and CI pipelines have been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.22.8, ensuring compatibility with the newer Go toolchain and taking advantage of its improvements and bug fixes.
enrichment.impact: Users who compile Kubernetes from source or rely on CI images will now use Go 1.22.8, which may provide better performance, security patches, and future‑compatibility. No runtime behavior changes for clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Ensure daemonset controller to count old unhealthy pods towards max unavailable budget
bugOrRegression.author: ncdc

enrichment.problem: During DaemonSet rolling updates the controller did not count already‑unhealthy old pods when computing the maxUnavailable budget, allowing more pods to be taken down than intended and risking service disruption.
enrichment.affected: Users running DaemonSets with a maxUnavailable budget, especially those whose pods can become unhealthy during updates.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller logic in kube‑controller‑manager was updated to include old unhealthy pods in the maxUnavailable calculation, ensuring the budget is respected throughout an update.
enrichment.impact: Updates to DaemonSets now honor the maxUnavailable limit even when some existing pods are unhealthy, preventing unexpected extra downtime and improving rollout reliability for workloads that use DaemonSets.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: When a Service has more than 1000 endpoint addresses, the endpoints controller truncates the list but fails to reconcile the Endpoint object, leaving stale or incomplete endpoint data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Services that generate more than 1000 endpoint addresses, such as large deployments or headless services, were affected by stale endpoint data.
enrichment.fix: The endpoints controller now correctly triggers a reconciliation after truncation, ensuring the Endpoint object is updated to reflect the truncated address set.
enrichment.impact: Services with a large number of pods (e.g., >1000) will now have accurate endpoint information, preventing traffic routing issues and ensuring high‑availability workloads function correctly.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
bugOrRegression.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: A memory leak existed in both kubelet and kube-apiserver when running with the default tracing configuration in Kubernetes 1.29, causing the processes to consume unbounded memory over time.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster running Kubernetes 1.29 with the default tracing configuration, affecting both node (kubelet) and control‑plane (kube-apiserver) components.
enrichment.fix: The leak was corrected in the kubelet and kube-apiserver code, ensuring that tracing-related resources are properly released and memory usage remains bounded under the default settings.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgraded to 1.29 will no longer experience gradual memory growth in the kubelet or API server, reducing the risk of OOM terminations, node instability, or API server unavailability and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression introduced in 1.29 where conntrack entries for UDP connections
  to deleted pods did not get cleaned up correctly, which could (among other things)
  cause DNS problems when DNS pods were restarted.
bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

enrichment.problem: A regression in v1.29 caused conntrack entries for UDP connections to pods that had been deleted to remain in the node's conntrack table. These stale entries prevented new UDP traffic from reaching the replacement pods, leading to DNS resolution failures when DNS pods were restarted.
enrichment.affected: Pods using UDP (especially kube-dns/CoreDNS pods) experienced DNS resolution failures after the pods were restarted or recreated.
enrichment.fix: The cleanup logic for conntrack entries was restored so that, upon pod deletion, any associated UDP conntrack entries are removed. This ensures that subsequent UDP connections (e.g., DNS queries) are correctly routed to the new pod instances.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable DNS functionality and prevents intermittent network failures for workloads that rely on UDP communication after pod restarts, reducing service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: ensure that Pods from the upgrade preflight check `CreateJob` are properly terminated after a timeout.
bugOrRegression.author: yuyabee

enrichment.problem: During a kubeadm upgrade, the preflight check creates a Job pod (CreateJob) that was not reliably terminated after its timeout, leaving stray pods that could block upgrades or waste resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters being upgraded with kubeadm; administrators running the upgrade preflight checks.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now tracks the timeout of the preflight Job and explicitly deletes the associated pod when the timeout expires, ensuring proper cleanup.
enrichment.impact: Upgrades with kubeadm will no longer hang or leave orphaned pods, improving upgrade reliability and preventing unnecessary resource consumption on the control plane nodes.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix wrong member list reported when removing an etcd member
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When removing an etcd member using kubeadm, the tool reported an incorrect list of etcd members, leading to inaccurate cluster state visibility.
enrichment.affected: Clusters created or managed with kubeadm where an etcd member is removed; operators relying on the reported member list.
enrichment.fix: Kubeadm now correctly regenerates and displays the updated etcd member list after a member removal operation.
enrichment.impact: Administrators get accurate etcd membership information, preventing confusion and potential mis‑management of the control‑plane etcd cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeadm join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When adding a new control‑plane node with `kubeadm join`, kubeadm would attempt to add the etcd member even if its peer URL was already present, causing duplicate member errors. Likewise, `kubeadm reset` tried to remove an etcd member without confirming the member ID existed, leading to removal failures.
enrichment.affected: Users adding or removing control‑plane nodes with `kubeadm join` or `kubeadm reset`. Clusters that already have the etcd member listed would previously encounter errors.
enrichment.fix: The join flow now checks the existing etcd member list and adds a member only if its URL is not already present. The reset flow now verifies the member ID before attempting removal, skipping the operation if the ID is absent.
enrichment.impact: Prevents join and reset operations from failing due to duplicate or missing etcd members, ensuring reliable control‑plane scaling and safe cluster teardown. This protects cluster stability and avoids potential etcd inconsistencies.

other.description: Kubeadm: removed `socat` and `ebtables` from kubeadm preflight checks
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: Kubeadm preflight checks required the presence of socat and ebtables binaries even when they were not needed, causing init/join to fail on systems that lacked these packages.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to bootstrap a cluster on nodes that do not have socat or ebtables installed.
enrichment.fix: The preflight validation has been updated to no longer check for socat and ebtables, allowing kubeadm init and join to succeed without them.
enrichment.impact: Users can now run kubeadm on minimal or hardened nodes without installing unnecessary networking tools, simplifying installation and reducing dependency overhead.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug when the hostname label of a node does not match the node name, pods bound to a PV with nodeAffinity using the hostname may be scheduled to the wrong node or experience scheduling failures.
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: When a node's hostname label (kubernetes.io/hostname) does not match the node's name, the scheduler could incorrectly evaluate nodeAffinity that references the hostname label, causing pods that are bound to a PersistentVolume to be placed on the wrong node or to fail scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Pods using PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity that reference the hostname label, and nodes where the hostname label does not match the node name.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler logic was updated to correctly handle cases where the hostname label differs from the node name, ensuring nodeAffinity based on the hostname label is evaluated against the actual label value rather than the node name.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on PersistentVolumes with nodeAffinity using the hostname label will now be scheduled to the intended node, preventing data access issues and unnecessary scheduling failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a suboptimal scheduler preemption behavior where potential preemption victims were violating Pod Disruption Budgets.
bugOrRegression.author: NoicFank

enrichment.problem: The scheduler’s preemption logic could select pods for eviction that would violate existing Pod Disruption Budgets, leading to unintended disruptions.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use preemption together with Pod Disruption Budgets; workloads protected by PDBs could be unintentionally evicted.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler preemption now checks Pod Disruption Budgets and avoids choosing victims that would cause a PDB violation.
enrichment.impact: Preemption respects disruption budgets, preventing unnecessary pod evictions and ensuring that availability guarantees defined by PDBs are upheld.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go compiler version, which can lack recent security patches, bug fixes, and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, CI pipelines, and downstream distributors of Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.22.9, ensuring all binaries are compiled with the latest supported Go release.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI systems that compile Kubernetes from source will benefit from improved build stability, security, and compatibility. End users receive binaries built with a more up‑to‑date toolchain, reducing potential upstream build‑related issues.

securityFixes.title: Command Injection affecting Windows nodes via nodes/*/logs/query API

A security vulnerability has been discovered in Kubernetes windows nodes
that could allow a user with the ability to query a node's '/logs' endpoint
to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

apiChange.description: NONE

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes builds were using an older Go version, which could miss upstream security fixes and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and users who compile or run Kubernetes binaries are affected, as the binaries are rebuilt with the new Go toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile the Kubernetes codebase with Go 1.22.10.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with a newer, supported Go release, improving overall security, stability, and compatibility with future Go updates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix kubelet on Windows fails if a pod has SecurityContext with RunAsUser
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: kubelet on Windows would fail to start a pod when the pod's spec included a SecurityContext with a RunAsUser field, causing pod creation errors.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes where pods specify a SecurityContext with RunAsUser were unable to launch those pods.
enrichment.fix: Added handling in the Windows kubelet to accept and correctly process SecurityContext.RunAsUser, preventing the failure and allowing the pod to start.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that need to run as a specific user can now be deployed without errors, improving reliability and compatibility of mixed OS clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a storage bug around multipath. iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices attached to nodes via multipath now resolve correctly if partitioned.
bugOrRegression.author: RomanBednar

enrichment.problem: When iSCSI or Fibre Channel devices were attached to a node using multipath and the underlying device was partitioned, the kubelet failed to correctly resolve the device, causing volume attachment/mount failures.
enrichment.affected: Nodes using iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage via multipath with partitioned devices; workloads that rely on those volumes.
enrichment.fix: The multipath resolution logic was updated so that partitioned iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices are correctly identified and resolved, allowing proper volume attachment and mounting.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage with multipath and partitioned devices will no longer experience volume mount errors, improving storage reliability for those workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a panic in kube-controller-manager handling StatefulSet objects when revisionHistoryLimit is negative
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager would panic and crash when it processed a StatefulSet that had a negative revisionHistoryLimit, causing the StatefulSet controller to stop reconciling those workloads.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that create or update StatefulSet objects with a negative revisionHistoryLimit. The panic previously affected the controller-manager process, disrupting StatefulSet management.
enrichment.fix: Added validation in the StatefulSet controller to handle a negative revisionHistoryLimit safely (treating it as zero) and prevent the panic.
enrichment.impact: Prevents controller-manager crashes for clusters with mis‑configured StatefulSets, ensuring StatefulSet updates and rollbacks continue to work and improving overall cluster stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: Fix the volume manager didn't check the device mount state in the actual state of the world before marking the volume as detached. It may cause a pod to be stuck in the Terminating state due to the above issue when it was deleted.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The kubelet volume manager marked volumes as detached without verifying the device's mount state in the actual state of the world, causing pods to remain in the Terminating phase after they were deleted.
enrichment.affected: Pods that were being deleted while using a volume on a node where the kubelet mis‑identified the volume state could become stuck in Terminating.
enrichment.fix: The volume manager now checks the device mount state before marking a volume as detached, ensuring proper volume cleanup and allowing pods to complete termination.
enrichment.impact: Pods can be terminated cleanly without getting stuck, improving reliability of workloads that use volumes and preventing resource leaks on nodes.

securityFixes.title: Node Denial of Service via Kubelet Checkpoint API
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a large number of container checkpoint requests made to the unauthenticated kubelet read-only HTTP endpoint may cause a Node Denial of Service by filling the Node's disk.

feature.description: Bump cAdvisor to v0.49.2
feature.author: cwangVT

enrichment.problem: cAdvisor version used by kubelet was outdated, potentially containing bugs or missing metric improvements.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running the default kubelet, especially workloads that rely on cAdvisor metrics for monitoring, autoscaling, or custom dashboards.
enrichment.fix: Update the embedded cAdvisor component to v0.49.2, bringing in upstream bug fixes, security patches, and metric enhancements.
enrichment.impact: Kubelet will provide more accurate and reliable container resource metrics, and any bugs addressed in the new cAdvisor release are resolved for clusters using the default kubelet configuration.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.11
feature.author: cpanato

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed the bug where the v1beta4 Timeouts.EtcdAPICall field was not respected in etcd client operations, and the default timeout of 2 minutes was always used.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: When using kubeadm with a v1beta4 ClusterConfiguration, the Timeouts.EtcdAPICall field is ignored, causing the etcd client to always use the hard‑coded 2‑minute timeout instead of the user‑specified value.
enrichment.affected: Users who configure a custom etcd API call timeout via kubeadm's v1beta4 ClusterConfiguration, particularly during kubeadm init or kubeadm join operations.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now respects the Timeouts.EtcdAPICall setting from the v1beta4 configuration, passing the configured timeout to etcd client operations.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on custom etcd API call timeouts (e.g., to speed up init/join when etcd is slow or unreachable) will now honor those settings, preventing unnecessary 2‑minute delays and improving cluster bootstrapping reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Added a feature gate `OrderedNamespaceDeletion`. When enabled, the pods resources are deleted before all other resources while namespace deletion to ensure workload security.
bugOrRegression.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: Namespace deletion could delete resources in an arbitrary order, potentially leaving non-pod resources (e.g., secrets, configmaps) that might be accessed after pods are gone, reducing workload security.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where namespaces are deleted, especially those handling sensitive workloads that require guaranteed pod cleanup before other resources.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `OrderedNamespaceDeletion` feature gate. When enabled, the deletion controller removes pod resources first before any other namespace-scoped resources, guaranteeing pods are terminated prior to other objects.
enrichment.impact: Provides a safer namespace teardown for clusters that need to ensure all workload pods are removed before other resources, reducing the risk of lingering resources being accessed after pod termination.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.30+ regression in connection stability for exec / attach / portforward requests initiated using a websocket client
bugOrRegression.author: fuweid

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.30 and later, exec, attach, and port‑forward operations that use a websocket client could experience unstable connections, causing commands to fail or streams to drop.
enrichment.affected: Developers and operators using kubectl exec, attach, or port‑forward against clusters running Kubernetes 1.30+.
enrichment.fix: The regression in the websocket handling path was corrected, restoring reliable connection stability for exec, attach, and port‑forward requests.
enrichment.impact: Users can again rely on kubectl exec, kubectl attach, and kubectl port‑forward for debugging and traffic tunneling without unexpected disconnections, improving developer productivity and operational stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic when no UpgradeConfiguration was found in the config file
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm panics (crashes) when the config file does not contain an UpgradeConfiguration section, causing the command to exit unexpectedly during upgrade operations.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using kubeadm upgrade with a config file that lacks an UpgradeConfiguration section.
enrichment.fix: Added a guard that checks for the presence of UpgradeConfiguration and returns a user‑friendly error instead of triggering a panic.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now run kubeadm upgrade commands with incomplete config files without the tool crashing, receiving a clear error message and avoiding interruption of upgrade workflows.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug where kube-apiserver could emit an further watch even even if decryption failed for earlier event and it was not emitted.
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: When kube-apiserver failed to decrypt a watch event, it could still emit subsequent watch events, causing clients to receive out‑of‑order or incomplete data and potentially miss the failed event.
enrichment.affected: Clients consuming the watch API (e.g., controllers, operators) that rely on encrypted resources could see missed or out‑of‑order events.
enrichment.fix: kube-apiserver now halts further watch emission after a decryption failure for an event, ensuring that no subsequent events are sent until the issue is resolved.
enrichment.impact: Improves consistency and reliability of the watch API for users employing encrypted resources, preventing silent data loss and ensuring correct event ordering.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix kubelet restart unmounts volumes of running pods if the referenced PVC is being deleted by the user
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When a node was restarted, the kubelet would unmount volumes from running pods if the pod's PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) was being deleted by the user at the same time, causing pod disruption and potential data loss.
enrichment.affected: Pods that have active PVC mounts on a node undergoing a restart while the PVC is being deleted.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now checks for PVC deletion during node restart and skips unmounting volumes that are still in use by running pods, preserving the volume mount until the pod terminates.
enrichment.impact: Running pods that rely on PVCs no longer lose their mounted volumes during node restarts, improving workload stability and preventing inadvertent data loss or pod failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Makes kubelet's /metrics/slis endpoint always available
bugOrRegression.author: richabanker

enrichment.problem: The kubelet /metrics/slis endpoint could be unavailable under certain conditions, causing gaps in Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics for monitoring systems.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster where monitoring relies on the kubelet's /metrics/slis endpoint; gaps previously impacted alerting and SLI dashboards.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now always exposes the /metrics/slis endpoint, ensuring that SLI metrics are consistently available for collection.
enrichment.impact: Users and monitoring tools can reliably scrape SLI metrics from every kubelet, improving observability and preventing silent monitoring gaps that could hide performance or reliability issues.
